output: Shopping may be resorted to under: (a) When there is an unforeseen contingency requiring immediate purchase, provided the amount shall not exceed Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000); or (b) Procurement of ordinary or regular office supplies and equipment not available in the Procurement Service involving an amount not exceeding Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P250,000), provided the Procurement does not result in splitting of contracts and at least three (3) price quotations from bona fide suppliers are obtained.

instruction: According to Section 53 of RA 9184, when shall Negotiated Procurement be allowed?
output: Negotiated Procurement shall be allowed only in: (a) cases of two failed biddings; (b) imminent danger to life or property during a state of calamity or when time is of the essence; (c) take-over of rescinded or terminated contracts where immediate action is necessary; (d) where the subject contract is adjacent or contiguous to an on-going infrastructure project under specific conditions; or (e) purchases of Goods from another government agency.

instruction: According to Section 55 of Republic Act No. 9184, how may decisions of the BAC be protested?
output: Decisions of the BAC in all stages of procurement may be protested to the head of the procuring entity and shall be in writing. Decisions of the BAC may be protested by filing a verified position paper and paying a non-refundable protest fee.

instruction: According to Section 57 of RA 9184, shall any protest stay or delay the bidding process?
output: No, in no case shall any protest taken from any decision stay or delay the bidding process. Protests must first be resolved before any award is made.

instruction: According to Section 59 of Republic Act No. 9184, how shall disputes arising from contract implementation be resolved?
output: Any and all disputes arising from the implementation of a contract covered by this Act shall be submitted to arbitration in the Philippines according to the provisions of Republic Act No. 876, otherwise known as the 'Arbitration Law.' Disputes within the competence of the Construction Industry Arbitration Commission shall be referred thereto. By mutual agreement, the parties may agree in writing to resort to alternative modes of dispute resolution.

instruction: According to Section 61 of RA 9184, are bid prices subject to price escalation during contract implementation?
output: For the given scope of work in the contract as awarded, all bid prices shall be considered as fixed prices, and therefore not subject to price escalation during contract implementation, except under extraordinary circumstances and upon prior approval of the GPPB.

instruction: According to Section 62(a) of Republic Act No. 9184, what is required from the contract awardee for goods procurement?
output: In order to assure that manufacturing defects shall be corrected by the supplier, manufacturer, or distributor for a specific time after performance of the contract, a warranty shall be required from the contract awardee for such period of time as may be provided in the IRR, the obligation for which shall be covered by either retention money or a special bank guarantee.

instruction: According to Section 62(b) of RA 9184, what is the contractor's responsibility for infrastructure projects?
output: The contractor shall assume full responsibility for the contract work from the time project construction commenced up to a reasonable period from its final acceptance by the government and shall be held responsible for any damage or construction of works except those occasioned by force majeure. The contractor shall undertake repair works, at his own expense, of any defect or damage on account of use of materials of inferior quality within ninety (90) days from the order to undertake repair.

instruction: Who are considered provisional members of the BAC and how are the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson designated?
output: Provisional BAC members include an officer with relevant technical expertise and knowledge of procurement, and a representative from the end-user or implementing unit with procurement knowledge. When procurement is outsourced to another GoP agency, a representative from the Procuring Entity may be designated as a provisional member. The Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson are designated by the Head of the Procuring Entity (HoPE), with the Vice-Chairperson being a regular BAC member.

instruction: What is the composition of the BAC for Local Government Units (LGUs)?
output: For provinces, cities, and municipalities, the BAC includes representatives from regular offices under the Local Chief Executive such as Administrator, Budget, Legal, Engineering, and General Services Offices, plus a representative from the end-user unit. The Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson are designated by the Local Chief Executive, with the Chairperson being at least the third ranking permanent official. For barangays, the BAC consists of 5 to 7 regular Sangguniang Barangay members, excluding the Punong Barangay, who designates the BAC leadership.

instruction: Who may serve as alternate BAC members and what are their roles?
output: The HoPE may designate alternate BAC members having the same qualifications as original members. Alternate members attend BAC meetings and receive proportionate honoraria when original members are absent and serve the same term as original members.

instruction: Can the HoPE or approving authority be BAC Chairperson or member?
output: No, the HoPE and/or approving authority cannot be the Chairperson or a member of the BAC under any circumstance.

instruction: What is the term of BAC members and conditions for replacement?
output: BAC members have a fixed one-year term renewable at the HoPE’s discretion. Upon term expiration, members continue their functions until successors are designated. Replacements serve only the unexpired term or duration of leave/suspension. Members may be suspended or removed by the HoPE for justifiable causes.

instruction: What are the primary functions of the BAC?
output: The BAC’s functions include advertising bids, conducting pre-procurement and pre-bid conferences, determining bidder eligibility, receiving and opening bids, evaluating bids, post-qualification, resolving reconsideration requests, recommending contract awards, imposing sanctions, recommending and conducting alternative procurement methods, assessing procurement processes, and creating Technical Working Groups for technical, legal, and financial assistance.

instruction: What responsibilities does the BAC have for procurement monitoring and reporting?
output: The BAC ensures the Procuring Entity complies with procurement laws and prepares the Procurement Monitoring Report (PMR) covering all projects in the APP from pre-procurement conference to contract approval. The PMR, approved by the HoPE, is submitted electronically to the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) within 14 calendar days after each semester and posted per executive orders.

instruction: What constitutes a quorum for BAC meetings and how can members attend?
output: A majority of total BAC members designated by the HoPE constitutes a quorum, requiring the presence of the Chairperson or Vice-Chairperson. Members, including Chair or Vice-Chair, may attend in person or via video/web conferencing if the Procuring Entity has such technology.

instruction: Who presides over BAC meetings and how are decisions made?
output: The Chairperson presides over BAC meetings, or the Vice-Chairperson if the Chairperson is absent. Meetings may be electronic where capability exists. Decisions by majority vote of quorum members present are binding; the Chairperson or Vice-Chairperson votes only to break ties.

instruction: Who are observers in the BAC proceedings and what are their qualifications?
output: At least two observers, in addition to a representative from the Commission on Audit (COA), are invited during key BAC activities. One observer must be from a recognized private group related to the procurement sector; the other from a non-government organization (NGO). Observers must be registered with SEC or CDA, have procurement expertise, no conflict of interest, and meet other BAC criteria.

instruction: What are the responsibilities of observers in BAC proceedings?
output: Observers prepare and submit reports on BAC compliance with procurement laws and suggest improvements to the HoPE, GPPB, and Ombudsman. Failure to submit reports within seven days implies the BAC followed correct procedures. Observers must immediately disclose any conflict of interest.

instruction: What documents can observers access and under what conditions?
output: Observers are granted free access to BAC meeting minutes, bid abstracts, post-qualification reports, APP/PPMP, and opened proposals upon request. They must sign a confidentiality agreement prescribed by the GPPB.

instruction: What is the role and composition of the BAC Secretariat/Procurement Unit?
output: The HoPE establishes a Secretariat to support the BAC, which may be an existing office. The Secretariat organizes meetings, manages procurement documents, advertises bids, assists procurement processes, monitors activities, consolidates PPMPs, prepares APPs, and facilitates communication among units and stakeholders.

instruction: What qualifications and priorities should the head and staff of the BAC Secretariat have?
output: The Secretariat Head in central offices must be at least a fifth ranking permanent employee, or third ranking in regional offices. Integrity and procurement proficiency are key factors for appointment. Members of the BAC, Secretariat, and TWG must prioritize procurement duties over other responsibilities until completion.

instruction: What provisions exist regarding honoraria for BAC, Secretariat, and TWG members?
output: The Procuring Entity may grant honoraria to BAC members not exceeding 25% of their basic monthly salary, subject to DBM guidelines. Honoraria may also be granted to Secretariat and TWG members following DBM rules.

instruction: How is professionalization of BAC, TWG, and Procurement Units promoted?
output: The GPPB provides ongoing training programs to develop capabilities and professionalize BAC, TWG, and Procurement Units. The HoPE ensures members complete authorized training within six months of designation and encourages HoPE participation in similar activities.

instruction: What key components must be included in Bidding Documents?
output: Bidding Documents must include ABC, Invitation to Bid, Eligibility Requirements, Instructions to Bidders, Terms of Reference, Scope of Work, Plans/Drawings, Technical Specifications, Form of Bid and Price Schedule, Delivery Schedule, Forms & Validity Period of Bid & Performance Security, Warranty, Contract Form, and General & Special Conditions of Contract.

instruction: When can a pre-procurement conference be waived or required?
output: Pre-procurement conferences are held prior to advertising bids, attended by BAC, Secretariat, and relevant officials. They confirm contract details and procurement readiness. They may be waived for small procurements below specified monetary thresholds for goods, infrastructure, or consulting services.

instruction: What information must the Invitation to Bid/Request for Expression of Interest contain?
output: It must state contract name, description of goods, project background, lots or items and evaluation basis, eligibility and evaluation criteria, dates and locations for submission and opening, ABC, source of funding, where to access bidding documents, contract duration or delivery schedule, contact information, and other relevant details. For electronic submission, it must state if allowed.

instruction: What are the requirements for advertising and posting the Invitation to Bid or Request for Expression of Interest according to the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The Invitation to Bid/Request for Expression of Interest must be posted at a conspicuous place in the Procuring Entity's premises for seven calendar days certified by the BAC Secretariat head, and continuously on the PhilGEPS website, the Procuring Entity’s website if available, and the website of the foreign funding source if applicable. Procuring Entities unable to post on PhilGEPS for justifiable reasons shall publish in a newspaper of general nationwide circulation.

instruction: Under what conditions must electronic bid submission certification be made and submitted?
output: If electronic bid submission is allowed, the highest IT official of the agency must issue a Certification per GPPB-prescribed form and submit it to the GPPB-Technical Support Office prior to posting Bidding Documents to allow electronic bid submission and receipt.

instruction: When is a pre-bid conference required and what are its main purposes under the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For contracts with an Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) of ₱1,000,000 or more, the BAC shall hold at least one pre-bid conference to clarify requirements, terms, conditions, and specifications. For contracts below this amount, pre-bid conferences may be at the BAC’s discretion or upon prospective bidder request. The pre-bid conference must be at least 12 calendar days before bid submission deadline and may be held electronically if technology permits.

instruction: What key topics are covered during a pre-bid conference?
output: Pre-bid conferences clarify eligibility requirements, technical and financial components, and address questions or clarifications from prospective bidders. Attendance is open but not mandatory, except for shortlisted bidders in consulting services procurement.

instruction: What are the procedures and timelines for issuing supplemental or bid bulletins?
output: Requests for clarifications must be in writing and submitted at least 10 calendar days before bid submission deadline. The BAC shall respond via Supplemental/Bid Bulletins signed by the BAC Chairperson and issued at least 7 calendar days before the deadline. These bulletins are posted on PhilGEPS, the Procuring Entity's website, and conspicuous places at premises. Bidders who submitted bids before issuance may modify or withdraw bids accordingly.

instruction: What documents are required for determining eligibility in the procurement of goods and infrastructure projects?
output: Eligibility documents include: Class “A” legal documents (registration from SEC/DTI/CDA, Mayor’s/Business permit, tax clearance), technical documents (statement of ongoing/completed contracts, Single Largest Completed Contract similar to the project), and financial documents (audited financial statements, NFCC or committed credit line). For Infrastructure Projects, a valid Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board license is required.

instruction: What flexibility exists regarding foreign bidders' eligibility and documentation requirements?
output: Foreign bidders’ documents and bids must be in English or accompanied by certified English translations authenticated by Philippine foreign service posts, except for Apostille Convention countries where apostille authentication applies. Foreign bidders may participate under treaties, reciprocal rights laws, lack of local suppliers, or to prevent anti-competitive situations.

instruction: What are the eligibility criteria for bidders in the procurement of goods?
output: Eligible bidders are duly licensed Filipino citizens/sole proprietorships; partnerships with ≥60% Filipino interest; corporations with ≥60% Filipino stock; cooperatives; or joint ventures with at least 60% Filipino ownership based on contributions specified in the joint venture agreements.

instruction: What are the specific eligibility requirements for infrastructure project bidders?
output: Bidders must be duly licensed Filipino citizens/sole proprietorships; partnerships with ≥60% Filipino interest; corporations with ≥60% Filipino capital stock; cooperatives; or joint ventures with ≥60% Filipino ownership, except specialized projects where ≥25% Filipino ownership suffices. PCAB licensing per R.A. 4566 is mandatory. Bidders must have completed a Single Largest Completed Contract similar in nature within specified periods, meeting at least 50% of the ABC, or follow Special provisions for Small A and B contractors.

instruction: How is the bidder’s Net Financial Contracting Capacity (NFCC) computed and what are its requirements?
output: NFCC is computed as [(current assets – current liabilities) x 15] minus the value of all outstanding/uncompleted projects. For domestic bidders, current assets/liabilities are based on audited financial statements submitted to the BIR; for foreign bidders, based on financial statements prepared under international standards. NFCC must be at least equal to the ABC to be bid. Alternatively, bidders may submit a committed line of credit equal to at least 10% of the ABC.

instruction: Under what conditions can the Procuring Entity review and disqualify a bidder post-eligibility?
output: The Procuring Entity may review a bidder's qualifications at any procurement stage if reasonable grounds exist to suspect misrepresentation or capability changes affecting eligibility. If found ineligible upon review, the bidder shall be disqualified from award or participation per IRR rules.

instruction: Who are the eligible participants for consulting services procurement?
output: Eligible participants include duly licensed Filipino citizens/sole proprietorships, partnerships with ≥60% Filipino interest, corporations with ≥60% Filipino capital stock, cooperatives, or joint ventures with ≥60% Filipino ownership. Consultants who will perform services must be Filipino and authorized registered professionals. Foreign consultants may be hired if Filipino consultants lack sufficient expertise as determined by the HoPE.

instruction: What documents are required for eligibility checking and shortlisting of consulting service bidders?
output: Documents include Class “A” legal documents (registration certificates, permits, tax clearance), technical documents (statements of ongoing and completed contracts, consultant nationality and professional registration), and financial documents (audited financial statements). Valid joint venture agreements or notarized statements from partners are required for joint ventures.

instruction: How is eligibility checked and shortlisting conducted for consulting services?
output: Eligibility envelopes are submitted before deadlines and opened to determine eligibility. The BAC evaluates documents per prescribed procedures, using PhilGEPS electronic registries to facilitate eligibility. Shortlisting considers similar contracts, consultant experience, qualification of personnel, workload, and number of shortlisted consultants (3-7, preferably 5). The shortlist is recommended to the HoPE for approval within 20 calendar days.

instruction: What review rights does the Procuring Entity have over consultants' qualifications after shortlisting?
output: The Procuring Entity reserves the right to review consultant qualifications during procurement if reasonable grounds indicate misrepresentation or capability changes. Consultants found non-compliant with eligibility criteria after review shall be disqualified in accordance with applicable IRR rules.

instruction: What is the objective and process of post-qualification in government procurement according to Section 34 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The post-qualification process verifies that the Lowest Calculated Bid or Highest Rated Bid complies with all bidding document requirements. The bidder must submit latest income and business tax returns and required permits within five calendar days upon notification. The BAC verifies the authenticity, validity, and accuracy of eligibility, technical, and financial documents using non-discretionary criteria. Failure to submit or falsification results in disqualification and possible forfeiture of bid security.

instruction: What documents must a bidder submit during post-qualification and what happens if these are not submitted on time?
output: The bidder must submit latest income and business tax returns, and other licenses or permits required and stated in the bidding documents within five calendar days of notification. Failure to submit these documents or a finding of falsity results in disqualification for award and forfeiture of the Bid Security per Section 69 of the IRR.

instruction: What specific criteria are considered during the post-qualification process for verifying a bidder’s compliance?
output: Criteria include legal requirements (licenses, permits, non-inclusion in blacklist), technical requirements (competence and experience, equipment availability, performance on ongoing contracts), verification and inspection of goods, and financial requirements (bid price, committed line of credit, or Net Financial Contracting Capacity). Deficiencies linked to bidder fault lead to disqualification.

instruction: What are the consequences if the first Lowest Calculated or Highest Rated Bidder fails post-qualification?
output: The BAC will notify the bidder in writing, initiate post-qualification of the next Lowest Calculated or Highest Rated Bidder, and repeat the process until a bidder passes or failure of bidding is declared.

instruction: Within what timeframe must the post-qualification process be completed?
output: Post-qualification shall be completed within twelve calendar days from the determination of the Lowest Calculated or Highest Rated Bidder. Under exceptional cases, the HoPE may extend this period but not beyond forty-five calendar days for goods and infrastructure projects or thirty calendar days for consulting services.

instruction: Under what circumstances will the BAC declare a bidding failure?
output: Bidding is declared a failure if no bids are received; all bidders are ineligible; all bids fail requirements or post-qualification; or the Lowest Calculated, Highest Rated, or Single Calculated/Rated Responsive Bidder refuses the award without justifiable cause.

instruction: What steps must the BAC take after a failure of bidding?
output: The BAC must review and evaluate the bidding documents and cost estimates, revise and adjust terms, conditions, specifications, and ABC as necessary, and conduct rebidding with readvertisement allowing initially eligible bidders to participate. After a second failure, the Procuring Entity may resort to negotiated procurement.

instruction: What are the rules regarding Single Calculated or Rated Responsive Bids in awarding contracts?
output: A Single Calculated and Responsive Bid or Single Rated and Responsive Bid may be awarded if it is the only bidder passing eligibility who submits a responsive bid, or if only one bidder submits a responsive bid after eligibility checks. The ABC must reflect the most advantageous prevailing price to the government.

instruction: What documents must the BAC submit to the Head of the Procuring Entity (HoPE) for contract award recommendation?
output: The BAC must submit the resolution recommending award, abstract of bids, approved program of work/delivery schedule and cost estimates, authorization document for incurring obligations, and other pertinent legal documents.

instruction: What is the timeframe for the HoPE to approve or disapprove the BAC contract award recommendation?
output: The HoPE or authorized representative has a maximum of fifteen calendar days from receipt of BAC’s recommendation to approve or disapprove the contract award.

instruction: What occurs if the HoPE disapproves the BAC's recommendation for contract award?
output: The HoPE must notify the BAC and the bidder in writing stating valid grounds for disapproval. The BAC then conducts post-qualification on the next Lowest Calculated or Highest Rated Bidder. The disapproved bidder may file a request for reconsideration within three calendar days, which the HoPE must resolve within seven calendar days. Reconsideration does not delay the bidding process and must be resolved before award.

instruction: What are the conditions a winning bidder must fulfill within ten days upon receipt of the Notice of Award?
output: The winning bidder must submit a valid joint venture agreement if applicable, a valid PCAB license or relevant SEC certificates for foreign bidders, post the required performance security, sign the contract, and obtain approval by higher authority if required.

instruction: How soon must the contract award be made following bid validity periods?
output: The contract award must be made within the bid validity period specified in the IRR.

instruction: Where and when must the Notice of Award be posted?
output: The BAC Secretariat shall post the Notice of Award within three calendar days of issuance on the PhilGEPS, Procuring Entity website if any, and conspicuous places within the Procuring Entity’s premises.

instruction: What is the process and timeline for contract signing after Notice of Award?
output: The winning bidder must post the required performance security and enter into contract within ten calendar days from receipt of Notice of Award. The Procuring Entity must sign the contract with the winning bidder within the same ten-day period, provided all documentary requirements are complied with.

instruction: What documents form part of the contract upon signing?
output: Contract documents include the Contract Agreement, Bidding Documents, winning bidder’s bid (eligibility, technical, and financial proposals), performance security, Notice of Award, and other legal documents such as construction schedules, manpower schedules, safety and health programs, and project scheduling tools.

instruction: What is the timeframe for higher authority approval of contracts?
output: Higher approving authorities have a maximum of twenty calendar days (or thirty calendar days for GOCC boards) from receipt of contracts to approve or disapprove them.

instruction: When must the Notice to Proceed be issued and what postings must follow?
output: The Procuring Entity must issue the Notice to Proceed along with approved contract copies within seven calendar days from contract approval. The BAC Secretariat must post the Notice to Proceed and approved contract on PhilGEPS and Procuring Entity’s website within fifteen calendar days from issuance.

instruction: What is the maximum allowable period for procurement activities from bid opening to award?
output: The procurement process from bid opening to contract award should not exceed three months, with the BAC members prioritizing procurement tasks until award. Specific activity periods and earliest possible times are provided, and deadlines falling on non-working days shift to the next working day unless exceptions for urgency are issued.

instruction: What are the requirements and forms of performance security?
output: Performance security must be posted prior to contract signing in forms such as cash, cashier’s/manager’s check, bank draft/guarantee, irrevocable letter of credit (confirmed if from foreign bank), or surety bond from certified insurance companies. Amounts are 5% for goods and consulting services, 10% for infrastructure projects, or 30% surety bond. Security must be in Philippine Pesos, forfeited upon default, valid until Certificate of Final Acceptance, and may reduce proportionally if contract value decreases.

instruction: What happens if a winning bidder fails to enter into contract or post performance security in time?
output: Failure to submit required documents or post performance security within stipulated times leads to forfeiture of bid security and imposition of sanctions unless failure is no fault of bidder. The BAC disqualifies the bidder and proceeds to post-qualification of next Lowest Calculated or Highest Rated Bidder until award or declaration of failure.

instruction: Under what grounds may the HoPE reject bids, declare failure, or not award the contract?
output: The HoPE may reject and declare failure based on prima facie evidence of collusion among officials or bidders, BAC procedural failures, or justifiable grounds such as significant project infeasibility, project no longer necessary, or withheld/reduced funding without Procuring Entity fault.

instruction: What guidelines apply to contract implementation, termination, and incentive bonuses?
output: Contract implementation guidelines are provided in Annexes D, E, and F for goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services respectively. Termination guidelines are in Annex I. Incentive bonuses are not allowed in any form or purpose.

instruction: What provisions exist regarding letters of credit for foreign suppliers?
output: Letters of credit must be issued by a Government Servicing Bank, with costs borne by the foreign supplier as stated in the bidding documents. Payment against letters of credit shall only occur after delivery and acceptance certified by the Procuring Entity.

instruction: According to Section 25.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, how shall bidders submit their bids?
output: Bidders shall submit their bids through their duly authorized representative using the forms specified in the Bidding Documents in two (2) separate sealed bid envelopes, or two (2) password-protected Bidding Documents in compressed archive folders in case of electronic bid submission, and which shall be submitted simultaneously. The first shall contain the technical component including eligibility requirements, and the second shall contain the financial component.

instruction: What documents must be included in the first envelope for procurement of Goods according to Section 25.2(a) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For procurement of Goods, the first envelope must contain: PhilGEPS Certificate of Registration and membership; Statement of all Ongoing Government and Private Contracts; Statement of SLCC; NFCC Computation or committed Line of Credit; JVA or Duly Notarized Statement if applicable; Bid security in prescribed form, amount and validity period; Technical Specifications; Omnibus Sworn Statement; and for foreign bidders claiming reciprocal rights, a certification from their government office.

instruction: According to Section 25.2(b) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what project requirements must be included for infrastructure projects?
output: For infrastructure projects, project requirements shall include: organizational chart for the contract to be bid; list of contractor's personnel with complete qualification and experience data; and list of contractor's major equipment units which are owned, leased, and/or under purchase agreements, supported by proof of ownership or certification of availability.

instruction: What must the Omnibus Sworn Statement contain according to Section 25.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The Omnibus Sworn Statement must contain: authorization of the signatory; that it is not blacklisted by the GoP or related entities; that documents are authentic, complete, and information is true; authorization for verification; compliance with disclosure provisions and labor laws; compliance with bidder responsibilities; that no commission or consideration was given to government officials; and acknowledgment of criminal liability for estafa in case of advance payment failure.

instruction: According to Section 25.5 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the maximum period from posting to bid submission for Goods?
output: For Goods, the maximum period from the last day of posting of the Invitation to Bid up to the submission and receipt of bids shall be forty-five (45) calendar days.

instruction: What are the maximum periods for Infrastructure Projects bid submission according to Section 25.5(b) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For Infrastructure Projects, the maximum periods are: fifty (50) calendar days for projects with ABC of Fifty million pesos and below, and sixty-five (65) calendar days for projects above fifty million pesos.

instruction: According to Section 25.5(c) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the maximum period for Consulting Services bid submission?
output: For Consulting Services, the maximum period from the last day of posting of the Request for Expression of Interest up to the submission and receipt of bids shall be seventy-five (75) calendar days.

instruction: What happens to bids submitted after the deadline according to Section 25.6 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Bids, including the eligibility requirements under Section 23.1, submitted after the deadline shall not be accepted by the BAC. The BAC shall record in the minutes the bidder's name, its representative and the time the late bid was submitted or generate a Bid receipt page for online submission showing the official time of late submission.

instruction: According to Section 25.7 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, when must the BAC Secretariat notify bidders of bid receipt?
output: To ensure transparency and accurate representation of the bid submission, the BAC Secretariat shall notify in writing all bidders whose bids it has received through its PhilGEPS-registered physical address or official e-mail address. The notice shall be issued within seven (7) calendar days from the date of the bid opening.

instruction: What happens to unsealed or unmarked bid envelopes according to Section 25.9 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Unsealed or unmarked bid envelopes, or in case of electronic bid submission, Bidding Documents not in compressed archive folders and not password-protected, shall be rejected. However, bid envelopes not properly sealed and marked or not properly compressed and password-protected shall be accepted, provided the bidder acknowledges such condition, and the BAC shall assume no responsibility for misplacement or premature opening.

instruction: According to Section 26.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, when may a bidder modify its bid?
output: A bidder may modify its bid, provided that this is done before the deadline for the submission and receipt of bids. The bidder shall not be allowed to retrieve its original bid, but shall only be allowed to send another bid equally sealed, properly identified, linked to its original bid and marked as a 'modification.'

instruction: Can a bidder withdraw its bid according to Section 26.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Yes, a bidder may, through a letter, withdraw its bid before the deadline for the receipt of bids. Withdrawal of bids after the applicable deadline shall be subject to appropriate sanctions. A bidder that withdraws its bid shall not be permitted to submit another bid, directly or indirectly, for the same contract.

instruction: According to Section 27.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the purpose of bid security?
output: All bids shall be accompanied by a bid security, payable to the Procuring Entity concerned as a guarantee that the successful bidder shall, within ten (10) calendar days from receipt of the notice of award, enter into contract with the Procuring Entity and furnish the performance security required in Section 39 of the IRR. Failure to enclose the required bid security shall automatically disqualify the bid.

instruction: According to Section 27.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the required amount for cash or cashier's check as bid security?
output: For cash or cashier's/manager's check issued by a Universal or Commercial Bank, the bid security amount shall be not less than two percent (2%) of the ABC. For biddings conducted by LGUs, the cashier's/manager's check may be issued by other banks certified by the BSP as authorized to issue such financial instrument.

instruction: What is the required bid security amount for surety bonds according to Section 27.2(c) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For a surety bond callable upon demand issued by a surety or insurance company duly certified by the Insurance Commission as authorized to issue such security, the bid security amount shall be not less than five percent (5%) of the ABC.

instruction: According to Section 27.4 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, when shall bid securities be returned?
output: Bid securities shall be returned only after the bidder with the Lowest Calculated Responsive Bid (LCRB) or Highest Rated Responsive Bid (HRRB) has signed the contract and furnished the performance security, except to those declared by the BAC as failed or post-disqualified upon submission of a written waiver of their right to file a request for reconsideration and/or protest.

instruction: What is a Bid Securing Declaration according to Section 27.5 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: A Bid Securing Declaration is an undertaking which states that the bidder shall enter into contract with the Procuring Entity and furnish the required performance security within ten (10) calendar days from receipt of the Notice of Award, and commits to pay the corresponding amount as fine and be automatically disqualified from bidding for a period of time upon receipt of the Blacklisting Order if it violates any conditions stated therein.

instruction: According to Section 28.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the maximum bid validity period?
output: Bids and bid securities shall be valid for a reasonable period as determined by the HoPE concerned, which shall be indicated in the Bidding Documents, but in no case shall the period exceed one hundred twenty (120) calendar days from the date of the opening of bids.

instruction: Can the bid validity period be extended beyond 120 days according to Section 28.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Yes, should it become necessary to extend the validity of the bids and bid securities beyond one hundred twenty (120) calendar days, the Procuring Entity shall request in writing all those who submitted bids for such extension before the expiration date. However, bidders shall have the right to refuse to grant such extension without forfeiting their bid security.

instruction: According to Section 29 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, when shall the BAC open the bids?
output: The BAC shall open the bids immediately after the deadline for the submission and receipt of bids. The time, date, and place of the opening of bids shall be specified in the Bidding Documents.

instruction: How are passwords disclosed for electronic bid submission according to Section 29 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For electronic bid submission, the passwords for accessing the Bidding Documents will be disclosed by the Bidders only during the actual bid opening which may be done in person or face-to-face through videoconferencing, webcasting or similar technology.

instruction: What happens if bids cannot be opened as scheduled according to Section 29 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: In case the bids cannot be opened as scheduled due to justifiable reasons, the BAC shall take custody of the bids submitted and reschedule the opening of bids on the next working day or at the soonest possible time through the issuance of a Notice of Postponement to be posted in the PhilGEPS website and the website of the Procuring Entity concerned.

instruction: According to Section 30.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what criterion does the BAC use during preliminary examination?
output: The BAC shall check the submitted documents of each bidder against a checklist of required documents to ascertain if they are all present, using a non-discretionary 'pass/fail' criterion, as stated in the Instructions to Bidders. If a bidder submits the required document, it shall be rated 'passed.' Bids that fail to include any requirement or are incomplete or patently insufficient shall be considered as 'failed.'

instruction: What must be submitted during post-qualification for electronic bid submissions according to Section 30.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For online or electronic bid submission, the bidder must submit the original copies of the bid securing declaration or other forms of bid security excluding cash, and the omnibus sworn statement to the BAC during the post-qualification stage. The non-submission of these forms on the set period shall render the bid submission as non-compliant and result in post-disqualification.

instruction: According to Section 30.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, when shall the second bid envelope be opened?
output: Immediately after determining compliance with the requirements in the first envelope, the BAC shall forthwith open the second bid envelope of each remaining eligible bidder whose first bid envelope was rated 'passed.' The second envelope of each complying bidder shall be opened within the same day, except as provided under Section 33 of the IRR.

instruction: What causes a bid to be rated as 'failed' according to Section 30.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: In case any of the requirements in the second envelope of a particular bid is missing, incomplete or patently insufficient, and/or if the submitted total bid price exceeds the ABC, the BAC shall rate the bid concerned as 'failed.' Only bids that contain all the bid requirements for both components shall be rated 'passed.'

instruction: What is two-stage bidding according to Section 30.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184?
output: A two-stage bidding procedure may be employed for procurement of Goods where the required technical specifications cannot be precisely defined in advance or where technically unequal bids are likely to occur. Prospective bidders submit eligibility requirements and initial technical proposals only at the first stage. The BAC evaluates technical merits, meets with eligible bidders to draw up final revised technical specifications, then bidders submit revised technical tenders and price proposals in the second stage.

instruction: According to Section 31.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the ABC in relation to bid prices?
output: The ABC shall be the upper limit or ceiling for acceptable bid prices. If a bid price, as evaluated and calculated in accordance with the IRR, is higher than the ABC, the bidder submitting the same shall be automatically disqualified. There shall be no lower limit or floor on the amount of the award.

instruction: Under what conditions may the ABC be applied for Foreign-funded Procurement according to Section 31.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For Foreign-funded Procurement, the ABC shall be applied as the ceiling provided that: Bidding Documents are obtainable free of charge on a freely accessible website; the Procuring Entity has procedures to ensure ABC is based on recent estimates; the Procuring Entity has trained cost estimators and quantity surveyors; the Procuring Entity has established systems to monitor bid prices and contract implementation. The GoP and foreign institution may agree to waive these conditions.

instruction: According to Section 32.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what communication is prohibited during bid evaluation?
output: Members of the BAC, its staff and personnel, Secretariat and TWG, as well as Observers, are prohibited from making or accepting any communication with any bidder regarding the evaluation of their bids until the issuance of the Notice of Award. However, the BAC, through its Secretariat, may ask in writing the bidder for a clarification of its bid. All responses to requests for clarification shall be in writing.

instruction: According to Section 32.2.1(a) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what happens if a required item has no price indicated?
output: Where a required item is provided but no price is indicated, the same shall be considered as non-responsive. However, specifying a zero (0) or a dash (-) for the said item would mean that it is being offered for free to the Government, except those required by law or regulations to be provided for.

instruction: According to Section 32.2.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, which prevails in case of discrepancy between bid prices in figures and words?
output: In case of discrepancies between bid prices in figures and in words, the latter shall prevail.

instruction: How are bids ranked according to Section 32.2.4 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184?
output: Bids shall then be ranked in the ascending order of their total calculated bid prices, as evaluated and corrected for computational errors, and other bid modifications, to identify the Lowest Calculated Bid. Total calculated bid prices which exceed the ABC shall be disqualified.

instruction: What must the Abstract of Bids contain according to Section 32.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The Abstract of Bids shall contain: name of the contract and its location if applicable; time, date and place of bid opening; and names of bidders and their corresponding calculated bid prices arranged from lowest to highest, the amount of bid security and the name of the issuing entity. All members of the BAC shall sign the Abstract of Bids.

instruction: According to Section 32.4 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, within what period must bid evaluation for Goods and Infrastructure be completed?
output: The entire evaluation process for the procurement of Goods and Infrastructure Projects shall be completed within seven (7) calendar days from the deadline for receipt of proposals.

instruction: What communication restrictions apply during consulting services evaluation according to Section 33.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: From submission and receipt of bids until the approval by the HoPE of the ranking of short listed bidders, those that have submitted their bids are prohibited from making any communication with any BAC member, including its staff and personnel, Secretariat and TWG, regarding matters connected to their bids. However, the BAC may ask in writing for clarification, and all responses shall be in writing.

instruction: According to Section 33.2.1.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, how does the Quality-Based Evaluation Procedure work?
output: A two-stage procedure is adopted whereby consultants submit technical and financial proposals simultaneously in separate sealed envelopes. Technical proposals are first opened and evaluated, consultants are ranked in descending order, and the Highest Rated Bid is identified provided it passes the minimum score. After HoPE approval, only the financial proposal of the Highest Rated Bid is opened for negotiations.

instruction: What are the weight requirements for Quality-Cost Based Evaluation according to Section 33.2.1.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Under Quality-Cost Based Evaluation, the financial proposal shall be given a minimum weight of fifteen percent (15%) up to a maximum of forty percent (40%). The weight of the technical criteria shall be adjusted accordingly such that their total weight together with the financial proposal weight shall add to one hundred percent (100%). The exact weights shall be approved by the HoPE and indicated in the Bidding Documents.

instruction: According to Section 33.2.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what criteria are used to evaluate technical proposals for consulting services?
output: Technical proposals shall be evaluated based on: quality of personnel to be assigned to the project covering suitability and qualifications of key staff; experience and capability of the consultant including records of previous engagement and quality of performance; and plan of approach and methodology with emphasis on clarity, feasibility, innovativeness and comprehensiveness of the approach.

instruction: According to Section 33.2.5 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what shall negotiations cover for consulting services?
output: Negotiations shall cover: discussion and clarification of terms of reference and scope of services; discussion and finalization of methodology and work program; consideration of appropriateness of qualifications and compensation of personnel; discussion on services, facilities and data to be provided by the Procuring Entity; discussion on the financial proposal; and provisions of the contract. Negotiations shall be completed within ten (10) calendar days except for meritorious reasons.

instruction: Can key personnel be replaced before contract award according to Section 33.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: There should be no replacement of key personnel before the awarding of contract, except for justifiable reason as determined by the BAC, such as illness, death, or resignation provided it is duly supported by relevant certificates, or any delay caused by the Procuring Entity. The BAC shall immediately consider negotiation with the next ranked consultant if unjustifiable replacement is made.

instruction: When can key personnel be replaced after contract award according to Section 33.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Once the contract has been awarded, no replacement shall be allowed by the HoPE until after fifty percent (50%) of the personnel's man-months have been served, except for justifiable reasons, subject to appropriate sanctions as prescribed in the PBDs.

instruction: According to Section 33.4 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, within what period must consulting services evaluation be completed?
output: The entire evaluation process, including the submission of the results to the HoPE for approval, shall be completed in not more than twenty-one (21) calendar days after the deadline for receipt of proposals. The proposal with the highest score shall be identified as the Highest Rated Bid.

instruction: What is the purpose of bid evaluation for Goods and Infrastructure Projects?
output: For the procurement of Goods and Infrastructure Projects, the purpose of bid evaluation is to determine the Lowest Calculated Bid by conducting detailed evaluation of financial components using non-discretionary criteria, correcting computational errors, and ranking bids from lowest to highest.

instruction: What happens if all taxes are not included in the bid?
output: All bidders shall be required to include the cost of all taxes, such as value added tax (VAT), income tax, local taxes, and other fiscal levies and duties which shall be itemized in the bid form and reflected in the detailed estimates. Such bids, including said taxes, shall be the basis for bid evaluation and comparison to ensure fair and competitive bid comparison.

instruction: How long does the HoPE have to approve the Highest Rated Bid for consulting services using Quality-Based Evaluation?
output: According to Section 33.2.1.1(iii) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, the HoPE shall approve or disapprove the recommendations of the BAC within two (2) calendar days after receipt of the results of the evaluation from the BAC.

instruction: When may oral presentations be required for consulting services procurement?
output: For complex or unique undertakings, such as those involving new concepts/technology or financial advisory services, participating short listed consultants may be required to make an oral presentation to be presented by each consultant or its nominated Project Manager within fifteen (15) calendar days after the deadline for submission of technical proposals.

instruction: What is the procurement policy on domestic and foreign goods preference under the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The Procuring Entity may procure goods from domestic or foreign sources, but shall give preference to domestically produced goods meeting the specified quality. The award will be made to the lowest Domestic Bidder whose bid does not exceed the lowest Foreign Bid by more than fifteen percent (15%). The Domestic Bidder must secure a certification from the DTI confirming substantial local composition of the goods.

instruction: How is the fifteen percent (15%) preference for domestic bidders applied during bid evaluation?
output: If the lowest Foreign Bid is lower than the lowest Domestic Bid, the Foreign Bid price is increased by fifteen percent (15%) for evaluation purposes. If the adjusted Foreign Bid price exceeds the Domestic Bid, the contract is awarded to the Domestic Bidder at the lowest Foreign Bid price. If the Domestic Bidder refuses to accept the contract at the Foreign Bid price within two calendar days of notice, the award goes to the Foreign Bidder.

instruction: What are the disqualification criteria related to relationships and conflicts for bidders under Section 47 of the 2016 IRR?
output: Bids must be accompanied by a sworn affidavit certifying the bidder is not related by consanguinity or affinity up to the third civil degree to the HoPE, BAC members, TWG, BAC Secretariat, PMO heads, end-user unit, or project consultants. Bidders related within this degree are automatically disqualified. Bidders with controlling shareholders in common, receiving subsidies from each other, sharing legal representatives, or having relationships allowing confidential information access or influence over other bids also face disqualification, among other conflict of interest cases.

instruction: What alternative methods of procurement are authorized under Rule XVI of the 2016 IRR and under what general conditions?
output: With prior HoPE approval and justified conditions, Procuring Entities may use alternative procurement methods to promote economy and efficiency, only in exceptional cases. Competitive bidding remains the general rule. Methods include limited source bidding, direct contracting, repeat order, shopping, negotiated procurement, agency-to-agency procurement, and others outlined in the rules, ensuring the most advantageous price to the government.

instruction: What is limited source bidding and when can it be used?
output: Limited source bidding or selective bidding involves direct invitation to bid to pre-selected suppliers or consultants known for experience and capability related to the contract. It is used for highly specialized goods or consulting services with few qualified suppliers, or for major plant components where uniform quality and performance maintenance are needed. The pre-selected list is maintained by relevant government authorities and updated regularly.

instruction: What is direct contracting and in what situations is it allowed?
output: Direct contracting is procurement without elaborate bidding documents, where the supplier is requested to submit a quotation or pro-forma invoice which may be accepted or negotiated immediately. It is allowed for proprietary goods obtainable only from a specific source, critical components ensuring contractor performance, or exclusive dealers with no suitable substitutes at better terms.

instruction: What are the conditions for repeat orders under the 2016 IRR?
output: Repeat orders are made from the previous winning bidder to replenish goods under previously awarded contracts, provided unit prices are the same or lower and still advantageous to the government. It cannot split contracts or exceed 25% of the original contract quantity. It must be within six months from the original Notice to Proceed, and the goods must be quantifiable, divisible, and consist of at least four units per item.

instruction: What is shopping as an alternative procurement method and its limitations?
output: Shopping involves requesting price quotations for readily available off-the-shelf goods or regular office supplies from known qualified suppliers. It is used for urgent procurements or small value goods not available in central procurement services, subject to thresholds prescribed in Annex H. At least three price quotations must be obtained. Office supplies exclude services like maintenance and security.

instruction: Under what conditions may negotiated procurement be resorted to?
output: Negotiated procurement is used in cases of two failed biddings, emergencies where immediate action is required to prevent damage or loss, contract take-over situations, procurement of adjacent or contiguous projects with same contractors, agency-to-agency procurement, scientific or exclusive work, hiring highly technical consultants, defense agreements, small value procurement, lease of real property and venue, NGO participation, community participation, and procurement from UN agencies or similar when advantageous to the government.

instruction: What are the procedures and limitations regarding protests on BAC decisions?
output: Requests for reconsideration must be filed within three calendar days of notice, answered within seven days, without allowing additional documents. Denied reconsiderations may be protested to the HoPE within seven days of resolution, accompanied by a non-refundable protest fee based on the ABC. Protests are resolved within seven days on records, decisions are final within approving authority limits, and protests do not delay bidding but must be resolved before award.

instruction: What administrative penalties can the Head of the Procuring Entity impose on bidders for violations under Rule XXIII of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA No. 9184?
output: The HoPE may impose suspension from participating in competitive bidding for one year for the first offense, and two years for the second offense, including disqualification from further participation for violations such as submission of false or falsified documents, withdrawal or refusal of award without justifiable cause, failure to post performance security, contract default, refusal to clarify bids, undue influence attempts, and habitual late or insufficient bids.

instruction: What happens to the bid or performance security of a bidder suspended or disqualified under administrative sanctions?
output: The bid security or performance security posted by the bidder shall be forfeited in addition to the suspension penalty.

instruction: What authority may the HoPE delegate to the BAC concerning administrative penalties?
output: The HoPE may delegate to the BAC the authority to impose administrative penalties such as suspension and disqualification on bidders.

instruction: Under what conditions may the HoPE issue preventive suspension against BAC members or personnel?
output: The HoPE may preventively suspend members of the TWG, Secretariat, or BAC if there is strong prima facie evidence or strong reasons showing the officials or employees are guilty of charges under Rules XXI and XXII or dishonesty under Civil Service Laws, observing due process.

instruction: What indemnification protections are provided to BAC members in the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: BAC members are entitled to an indemnification package that includes free legal assistance, liability insurance, and coverage of reasonable fees and expenses for actions arising from lawful performance of duties unless found liable for gross negligence or misconduct. They are also entitled to medical assistance for injuries incurred during official functions.

instruction: How may the 2016 Revised IRR be amended and when do such amendments apply?
output: The GPPB may amend this IRR as needed. Any amendments apply to all procurement activities with advertisements or invitations issued after the amendment's effectivity date.

instruction: What previous orders and issuances does the 2016 Revised IRR repeal or modify?
output: The IRR repeals Executive Orders 40, 262, 201, and 302; Presidential Decree 1594; relevant portions of R.A. 7898 and E.O. 164; Memorandum Order 119 (2003); GPPB Resolution 03-2009; and relevant portions of E.O. 301, among others, including any laws inconsistent with the IRR.

instruction: What is the transitory clause about the applicability of earlier procurement laws?
output: Procurement activities with advertisements or invitations issued before the IRR’s effectivity shall follow prior applicable laws such as E.O. 40, P.D. 1594, R.A. 7160, or other rules in force. Procuring Entities may continue procedures under the 2009 Revised IRR or other laws for such procurements.

instruction: When does the 2016 Revised IRR take effect?
output: The IRR takes effect sixty (60) calendar days after publication in the Official Gazette or a nationwide circulation newspaper and upon filing three certified copies with the University of the Philippines Law Center.

instruction: What activities are included in detailed engineering for infrastructure projects according to Annex A?
output: Detailed engineering includes survey, site investigation, soils and foundation investigation, construction materials investigation, preparation of design plans, technical specifications, quantity and cost estimates, program of work, construction schedule with cash flow estimates, right-of-way plans, utility relocation plans, design reports, environmental impact statements for critical projects, construction safety and health program requirements, value engineering, and bid/tender document preparation.

instruction: What standards and practices govern design standards and surveys in detailed engineering?
output: Design standards follow agency-adopted accepted detailed engineering practices considering seismicity for structural safety. Field surveys include aerial, hydrographic, topographic, hydrologic, sub-surface, and monumenting surveys conducted per agency criteria, aimed at producing plans enabling quantity estimates within ±10% accuracy.

instruction: What contract plans and quantity computations are required in detailed engineering?
output: Contract plans include site development, plan/profile sheets, typical sections, drainage and structural details, and other required drawings. Quantities must be computed within ±10% accuracy of as-built structures. Special provisions for work methods and unit prices based on approved current costs, divided into local and foreign currency components, shall be prepared.

instruction: What requirements must the Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) meet in infrastructure projects?
output: The ABC must be prepared and approved by designated Procuring Entity officials and consider projected inflation and foreign exchange rates over the construction period. It should detail local and foreign currency requirements and specify equipment rentals, fuel, labor, materials, overhead, safety program, and warranty premium costs.

instruction: What are the requirements for program of work, contract time, and warranty periods in infrastructure projects?
output: A program of work must be approved before commencing construction and include cost estimates and a PERT/CPM network. Contract time estimates account for working days adjusted for holidays and average unworkable days based on PAGASA data, disclosed in instructions to bidders. Warranty periods and value engineering requirements are specified by the procuring entity in bidding documents.

instruction: What certification must consultants or officials give regarding detailed engineering surveys and designs?
output: Consultants and officials must certify that detailed engineering surveys and designs comply with agency standards and specifications and are adequate for procurement. Approval does not lessen consultant responsibility for technical integrity nor transfer it to approving officials.

instruction: How are detailed engineering provisions adapted during emergency or extraordinary situations?
output: In emergencies or major calamities declared by the President, detailed engineering shall follow agency-approved guidelines enabling quick response while maintaining safety and structural integrity, as approved by the Infrastructure Committee of the NEDA Board.

instruction: How are consultants defined and classified under Annex B of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Consultants are natural or juridical persons qualified by education, training, and experience to provide specified consulting services under this IRR. Services are divided into six categories: advisory/review, pre-investment/feasibility studies, design, construction supervision, management and related services, and other technical or special studies.

instruction: What obligations ensure consultant independence and professionalism?
output: Consultants and key staff associated with non-consulting firms must limit their role to consultancy and disqualify themselves and affiliates from bidding on project products or services to avoid conflicts of interest, preserving independence, integrity, and objectivity.

instruction: What is the hiring basis for consultants and preference for Filipino consultants?
output: Consultants are hired based on proven expertise, experience, and capability. Filipino consultants shall be hired when capable; foreign consultants may be hired when Filipinos lack expertise as determined by the Head of the Procuring Entity, following Philippine laws. Technology and knowledge transfer must be included where applicable.

instruction: What role does the umbrella organization of consultants play?
output: The umbrella organization accredits consultants technically and financially, maintains updated lists of qualified consultants, regulates the industry, and serves as a consultative body with government agencies. GPPB recognizes this organization, which submits accredited consultants to BACs as registries, guiding eligibility determinations.

instruction: What are the main categories of consulting services defined in the IRR?
output: Consulting services comprise advisory and review services; pre-investment or feasibility studies; design; construction supervision; management and related services; and other technical or special studies including institution building, technical training, economic studies, and specialized inspections or litigation support.

instruction: According to Section 59.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what must parties do if a dispute arises during contract implementation?
output: If any dispute or difference of any kind whatsoever shall arise between the parties in connection with the implementation of the contract, the parties shall make every effort to resolve amicably such dispute or difference by mutual consultation.

instruction: According to Section 59.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, where shall disputes from contract implementation be submitted?
output: Any and all disputes arising from the implementation of a contract shall be submitted to arbitration in the Philippines according to the provisions of R.A. 876, otherwise known as the 'Arbitration Law' and R.A. 9285, otherwise known as the 'Alternative Dispute Resolution Act of 2004.' However, disputes within the competence of the Construction Industry Arbitration Commission shall be referred thereto.

instruction: Can parties agree to use alternative dispute resolution methods according to Section 59.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Yes, the process of arbitration shall be incorporated as a provision in the contract, provided further that by mutual agreement, the parties may agree in writing to resort to other alternative modes of dispute resolution.

instruction: According to Section 60 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, how may arbitral awards be appealed?
output: The arbitral award and any decision rendered in accordance with Section 59 shall be appealable by way of a petition for review to the Court of Appeals. The petition shall raise pure questions of law and shall be governed by the Rules of Court.

instruction: According to Section 61.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, are bid prices subject to price adjustment during contract implementation?
output: For the given scope of work in the contract as awarded, all bid prices shall be considered as fixed prices, and therefore not subject to price adjustment and escalation during contract implementation, except under extraordinary circumstances and upon prior approval of the GPPB, or when a Treaty or International or Executive Agreement expressly allows it.

instruction: According to Section 61.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, when shall contract price adjustment be made?
output: In cases where the cost of the awarded contract is affected by any applicable new laws, ordinances, regulations, or other acts of the GoP, promulgated after the date of bid opening, a contract price adjustment shall be made or appropriate relief shall be applied on a no loss-no gain basis.

instruction: Who determines extraordinary circumstances for price escalation according to Section 61.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Any request for price escalation under extraordinary circumstances shall be submitted by the concerned entity to the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) with the endorsement of the Procuring Entity. For purposes of this Section, 'extraordinary circumstances' shall refer to events that may be determined by the NEDA in accordance with the Civil Code of the Philippines, and upon the recommendation of the Procuring Entity concerned.

instruction: According to Section 61.4 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, in what currency shall contracts be denominated?
output: All contracts shall be denominated and payable in Philippine currency, and this shall be stated in the Bidding Documents. However, subject to GPPB guidelines, the Procuring Entity may provide in the Bidding Documents that obligations may be paid in foreign currency which shall be accepted or tradeable by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.

instruction: According to Section 62.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the minimum warranty period for Expendable Supplies?
output: For the procurement of Goods, a warranty security shall be required from the contract awardee for a minimum period of three (3) months in the case of Expendable Supplies, after acceptance by the Procuring Entity of the delivered supplies.

instruction: What is the minimum warranty period for Non-expendable Supplies according to Section 62.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For the procurement of Goods, a warranty security shall be required from the contract awardee for a minimum period of one (1) year in the case of Non-expendable Supplies, after acceptance by the Procuring Entity of the delivered supplies.

instruction: According to Section 62.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what forms may warranty security take for goods procurement?
output: The obligation for the warranty shall be covered by either retention money in an amount equivalent to at least one percent (1%) but not to exceed five percent (5%) of every progress payment, or a special bank guarantee equivalent to at least one percent (1%) but not to exceed five percent (5%) of the total contract price.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the contractor's responsibility from project construction to final acceptance?
output: From the time project construction commenced up to final acceptance, the contractor shall assume full responsibility for: any damage or destruction of the works except those occasioned by force majeure; and safety, protection, security, and convenience of his personnel, third parties, and the public at large, as well as the works, equipment, installation and the like to be affected by his construction work.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.2.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, within how many days must a contractor undertake repair works for defects?
output: The contractor shall undertake the repair works, at his own expense, of any damage to the infrastructure on account of the use of materials of inferior quality, within ninety (90) days from the time the HoPE has issued an order to undertake repair.

instruction: What happens if a contractor fails to comply with repair obligations according to Section 62.2.2.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: In case of failure or refusal to comply with the mandate to undertake repair, the Procuring Entity shall undertake such repair works and shall be entitled to full reimbursement of expenses incurred therein upon demand.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.2.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what covers the defects liability period?
output: The defects liability period shall be covered by the Performance Security of the contractor required in Section 39.1 of the IRR, which shall guarantee that the contractor performs his responsibilities. If the contractor fails to comply with its obligations, the Procuring Entity shall forfeit its performance security, subject its property to attachment or garnishment proceedings, and perpetually disqualify it from participating in any competitive bidding.

instruction: Who may be held responsible for Structural Defects or Failures according to Section 62.2.3.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The following may be held responsible for Structural Defects or Failures: Contractor for improper construction or use of inferior materials; Consultants for faulty design or inadequate construction supervision; Procuring Entity's Representatives for willful intervention or negligence; Third Parties for work they undertook that caused defects; and Users for abuse/misuse of the constructed facility.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.3.2(a) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the warranty period for Permanent Structures?
output: The warranty against Structural Defects and Failures for Permanent Structures shall cover fifteen (15) years from final acceptance, except those occasioned by force majeure. This includes Buildings of types 4 and 5 and other structures made of steel, iron, or concrete such as steel/concrete bridges, flyovers, aircraft movement areas, ports, dams, tunnels, filtration and treatment plants, sewerage systems, power plants, and other similar permanent structures.

instruction: What is the warranty period for Semi-Permanent Structures according to Section 62.2.3.2(b) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The warranty against Structural Defects and Failures for Semi-Permanent Structures shall cover five (5) years from final acceptance. This includes Buildings of types 1, 2, and 3, concrete/asphalt roads, concrete river control, drainage, irrigation lined canals, river landing, deep wells, rock causeway, pedestrian overpass, and other similar semi-permanent structures.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.3.2(c) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the warranty period for Other Structures?
output: The warranty against Structural Defects and Failures for Other Structures shall cover two (2) years from final acceptance. This includes Bailey and wooden bridges, shallow wells, spring developments, and other similar structures.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.3.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the required warranty security amount for cash or letter of credit?
output: For cash or Letter of Credit issued by a Universal or Commercial Bank, the warranty security amount shall be not less than five percent (5%) of the Total Contract Price. The Letter of Credit shall be confirmed or authenticated by a Universal or Commercial Bank if issued by a foreign bank.

instruction: What is the required warranty security amount for bank guarantee according to Section 62.2.3.3(b) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: For bank guarantee confirmed by a Universal or Commercial Bank, the warranty security amount shall be not less than ten percent (10%) of the Total Contract Price. For biddings conducted by LGUs, the bank guarantee may be issued by other banks certified by the BSP.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.3.3(c) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what is the required warranty security amount for surety bonds?
output: For surety bond callable upon demand issued by GSIS or a surety or insurance company duly certified by the Insurance Commission as authorized to issue such security, the warranty security amount shall be not less than thirty percent (30%) of the Total Contract Price.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.3.4 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, how long shall warranty security remain effective?
output: The warranty security shall be denominated in Philippine Pesos, remain effective for one (1) year from the date of issuance of the Certificate of Final Acceptance by the Procuring Entity, and returned only after the lapse of the said one (1) year period.

instruction: According to Section 62.2.4 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what happens if Structural Defects occur during the warranty period?
output: In case of Structural Defects/Failure occurring during the applicable warranty period, the Procuring Entity shall undertake the necessary restoration or reconstruction works and shall be entitled to full reimbursement by the parties found to be liable for expenses incurred therein upon demand, without prejudice to filing appropriate administrative, civil, and/or criminal charges and forfeiture of warranty securities.

instruction: According to Section 63.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what are the duties and responsibilities of the GPPB?
output: The GPPB shall: protect national interest in public procurement matters; formulate and amend public procurement policies, rules and regulations; prepare generic procurement manual and standard bidding forms; ensure proper implementation by Procuring Entities; establish sustainable training programs; and conduct annual reviews of the Act's effectiveness and recommend amendments.

instruction: What is the GPPB Technical Support Office according to Section 63.2 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The GPPB shall create a Technical Support Office (TSO) which shall provide support in the performance of its duties and responsibilities. The TSO shall be an attached agency of the DBM and shall be under its administrative supervision for general oversight and budgeting purposes. The TSO shall be headed by an Executive Director appointed by the President.

instruction: According to Section 63.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what support does the TSO provide to the GPPB?
output: The TSO shall provide: research-based procurement policy recommendations and rule-drafting; development and updating of generic procurement manuals and standard bidding forms; management and conduct of training; evaluation of the effectiveness of the government procurement system; monitoring compliance and assisting Procuring Entities; monitoring the implementation of PhilGEPS; and secretariat support.

instruction: According to Section 64 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, who composes the GPPB?
output: The GPPB shall be composed of the Secretary of the Department of Budget and Management as Chairperson, the Director-General of NEDA as Alternate Chairperson, with the Secretaries of DPWH, Finance, Trade and Industry, Health, National Defense, Education, DILG, Science and Technology, Transportation, DICT, and Energy as Members, the Director-General of Philippine Space Agency, and a private sector representative appointed by the President. The GPPB may invite COA representatives or relevant agencies as resource persons.

instruction: According to Section 65.1(a) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what offense is committed by opening sealed bids prematurely?
output: Public officers who open any sealed bid including bids submitted through the electronic system and any documents required to be sealed or divulging their contents, prior to the appointed time for the public opening of bids, shall suffer the penalty of imprisonment of not less than six (6) years and one (1) day, but not more than fifteen (15) years.

instruction: What offense is committed by delaying procurement activities according to Section 65.1(b) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
