output: Public officers who delay, without justifiable cause, the screening for eligibility, opening of bids, evaluation and post evaluation of bids, and awarding of contracts beyond the prescribed periods of action provided for in the IRR shall suffer the penalty of imprisonment of not less than six (6) years and one (1) day, but not more than fifteen (15) years.

instruction: According to Section 65.1(d) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what offense involves splitting of contracts?
output: Public officers who split contracts which exceed procedural purchase limits to avoid competitive bidding or to circumvent the limits of approving or procurement authority shall suffer the penalty of imprisonment of not less than six (6) years and one (1) day, but not more than fifteen (15) years.

instruction: What additional penalties are imposed when private individuals collude with public officers according to Section 65.1 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: When any of the foregoing acts is done in collusion with private individuals, the private individuals shall likewise be liable for the offense. The public officer involved shall suffer temporary disqualification from public office, while the private individual shall be permanently disqualified from transacting business with the Government.

instruction: According to Section 65.2(a) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what constitutes bid collusion?
output: When two or more bidders agree and submit different bids as bona fide bidders, all the while knowing that the bid(s) of one or more of them was so much higher than the other that the latter could not be honestly accepted and that the contract will surely be awarded to the pre-arranged lowest bid, they shall suffer imprisonment of not less than six (6) years and one (1) day but not more than fifteen (15) years.

instruction: What offense is committed by submitting multiple bids through different entities according to Section 65.2(b) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: When a bidder maliciously submits different bids through two or more persons, corporations, partnerships or any other business entity in which he has an interest, to create the appearance of competition that does not in fact exist so as to be adjudged as the winning bidder, shall suffer imprisonment of not less than six (6) years and one (1) day but not more than fifteen (15) years.

instruction: According to Section 65.3(a) of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what offense involves false eligibility documents?
output: Private individuals who submit eligibility requirements that contain false information or falsified documents calculated to influence the outcome of the eligibility screening process or conceal information that would lead to ineligibility, and any public officer conspiring with them, shall suffer imprisonment of not less than six (6) years and one (1) day but not more than fifteen (15) years.

instruction: What offense is committed by withdrawing a qualified bid according to Section 65.3(d) of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Withdrawing a bid after it shall have qualified as the Lowest Calculated Bid/Highest Rated Bid, or refusing to accept an award without just cause or for the purpose of forcing the Procuring Entity to award the contract to another bidder, including non-submission or delaying submission of performance security, shall result in imprisonment of not less than six (6) years and one (1) day but not more than fifteen (15) years.

instruction: According to Section 65.5 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, who bears criminal liability when the bidder is a juridical entity?
output: When the bidder is a juridical entity, criminal liability and the accessory penalties shall be imposed on its directors, officers or employees who actually commit any of the foregoing acts. If a person previously held liable has a controlling interest in a prospective bidder-entity, the said bidder-entity shall be disqualified to participate in any procurement activity being conducted by the Government.

instruction: According to Section 66 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, which courts have jurisdiction over procurement offenses?
output: Jurisdiction over the offenses defined under Rule XXI shall belong to the appropriate courts, according to laws existing at the time of the commission of the offenses.

instruction: According to Section 67 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what civil liability accompanies conviction under procurement laws?
output: Without prejudice to administrative sanctions, a conviction under the Act and the IRR or R.A. 3019 shall carry with it civil liability, which may either consist of restitution for the damage done or the forfeiture in favor of the government of any unwarranted benefit derived from the act or acts in question, or both, at the discretion of the courts.

instruction: According to Section 68 of the 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184, what are liquidated damages?
output: All contracts executed shall contain a provision on liquidated damages which shall be payable by the contractor in case of breach. For the procurement of Goods, Infrastructure Projects and Consulting Services, the amount shall be at least equal to one-tenth of one percent (0.001) of the cost of the unperformed portion for every day of delay.

instruction: When may a contract be rescinded due to liquidated damages according to Section 68 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Once the cumulative amount of liquidated damages reaches ten percent (10%) of the amount of the contract, the Procuring Entity may rescind or terminate the contract, without prejudice to other courses of action and remedies available under the circumstances.

instruction: What is the burden of proof for price escalation requests according to Section 61.3 of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The burden of proving the occurrence of extraordinary circumstances that will allow for price escalation shall rest with the entity requesting for such escalation. NEDA shall only respond to such request after receiving the proof and the necessary documentation.

instruction: What action should parties take before resorting to arbitration?
output: If any dispute or difference arises between the parties in connection with contract implementation, the parties shall make every effort to resolve amicably such dispute or difference by mutual consultation before resorting to arbitration.

instruction: What are the guidelines for amendments to orders in the procurement of goods, supplies, and materials according to Annex D of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Amendments to orders may be issued at any time by the Procuring Entity if they involve cost or time changes, subject to mutual agreement and written contract modification. Amendments apply only in emergencies or fortuitous events affecting drawings, shipment method, packing, or delivery place. Additional items necessary for goods' protection not in the original contract may also be added, with payments based on original or mutually agreed unit prices. Work under amendment must be approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity or authorized representative, except Regional Directors may authorize immediate work start for emergencies if cost increases do not exceed 5% cumulatively, with proper approval documentation.

instruction: What conditions and procedures surround suspension of work under the 2016 Revised IRR for goods procurement?
output: The Procuring Entity may suspend work wholly or partly by written order due to force majeure or fortuitous events. The supplier must minimize costs during suspension. Before suspension expires, the order must be lifted or the work terminated. Upon lifting, the supplier resumes work with adjustments to delivery or contract schedules or price as applicable, with contract modifications reflecting changes.

instruction: What are the liquidated damages provisions for delayed delivery in goods procurement under the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Liquidated damages of 0.1% of the cost of delayed goods per day apply for unsatisfactory delivery within the schedule, including extensions. The Procuring Entity need not prove actual damage. Deductions may be from payments or posted securities. If total damages reach 10% of contract price, the Procuring Entity may rescind the contract and impose additional sanctions.

instruction: What are the rules for advance payments in the procurement of goods under the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: Advance payments up to 15% of contract amount require prior Presidential approval, except for specific services and calamity contingencies. Progress payments offset the advance payment until exhausted unless otherwise approved. Up to 50% advance payment is allowed for hotels, conference use, and office leases. For calamities with declared State of Calamity, 15% advance payment is allowed without prior approval.

instruction: What general contract implementation aspects are covered in the manuals to be issued by the GPPB for goods procurement?
output: Manuals cover incidental services, spare parts, delays in supplier performance, purchaser responsibilities, prices, payment, taxes and duties, subcontracts, standards, packing, insurance, transportation, inspections and tests, patent rights, limitations of liability, termination for default, insolvency, convenience, and assignment.

instruction: What are variation orders and change orders in infrastructure procurement according to Annex E?
output: Variation Orders cover increases/decreases in work quantities or new work items within general project scope due to plan or field condition changes. Change Orders cover quantity adjustments in original work items. Extra Work Orders cover new necessary work not in the original contract, such as latent site conditions. Additive Variation Orders are limited to a cumulative 10% of the original contract price, with provisions for exceptional extensions up to 20% under urgent cases.

instruction: What procedures govern the preparation and approval of variation orders in infrastructure projects?
output: The procuring entity’s representative prepares proposed Change or Extra Work Orders with detailed quantities, inspections, and cost estimates, submitting them to the Head of Procuring Entity. Technical staff investigates and reports findings for approval. The Head or authorized representative approves justified Variation Orders. Processing from preparation to approval must not exceed 30 calendar days.

instruction: How are additional or extra work costs priced in infrastructure projects?
output: Additional work with existing contract work uses original unit prices. For new work items, unit prices are based on direct unit costs (materials, labor, equipment) estimated by the contractor and validated via documented canvass. The cost combines direct costs with the contractor’s mark-up (taxes and profit), mutually acceptable to government and contractor. Payment requests must be accompanied by detailed supporting statements.

instruction: When can contractors start work under variation orders, and what payments may be made?
output: Contractors cannot start work under Change/Extra Work Orders without prior approval by the Head of Procuring Entity, except in emergencies or when time is critical, subject to fund availability and cumulative unapproved work not exceeding 5% of adjusted original contract price. Payments for satisfactorily completed variation work require such approval.

instruction: What are the payment and progress payment procedures for infrastructure projects under Annex E?
output: Advance payments up to 15% may be made against an irrevocable standby letter of credit, bank guarantee, or surety bond. Contractors repay advance payments by deducting proportional amounts from progress payments. Progress payments require monthly statements of work accomplished, certified by procuring entity representatives, excluding undelivered materials. Deductions include previous payments, advance payment recovery, retention money, third-party liabilities, and uncorrected defects.

instruction: What is retention money, its application, and possible substitution in infrastructure contracts?
output: Ten percent (10%) of progress payments is retained as retention money until 50% of work value completion, after which retention may cease if work is satisfactory and on schedule. Retention is released upon final acceptance. Contractors may substitute retention money with irrevocable standby letters of credit, bank guarantees, or surety bonds, valid for a period covering defect liabilities and liabilities to third parties, subject to satisfactory project progress.

instruction: How is contract completion and negative slippage monitored and managed in infrastructure projects?
output: Upon reaching 95% completion, an inspectorate team issues a punch-list of deficiencies and deadlines for completion. The Procuring Entity monitors contractor performance to ensure timely project implementation. Negative slippage triggers calibrated measures per GPPB Circular 03-2019 for contract termination guidance if slippage reaches 15%.

instruction: What are the provisions on liquidated damages for late completion in infrastructure contracts?
output: If the contractor fails to complete work satisfactorily after contract duration plus granted extensions, liquidated damages of at least 0.1% per day of the unperformed work cost apply. Project usability certification by end-users determines applicability. Damages are deducted from payments or securities. If damages reach 10% of contract price, the Procuring Entity may terminate the contract, forfeit performance security, and either take over or re-procure under alternative methods.

instruction: Under what conditions may work be suspended in infrastructure projects?
output: The Procuring Entity may suspend work wholly or partly for force majeure, fortuitous events, unsafe conditions, valid orders, or contract provisions. Contractors must comply immediately. Contractors may suspend work after 15 days' notice for critical issues like right-of-way problems, missing owner-furnished plans, dangerous peace and order situations certified by authorities, failure to deliver government-furnished materials, or delayed progress payments beyond 45 days unless justified.

instruction: When and how is extension of contract time granted in infrastructure procurement?
output: Extensions are granted if additional work or special circumstances justify delays, provided the contractor submits notice within 30 calendar days of occurrence. Extensions are not given for ordinary unfavorable weather or contractor negligence in providing resources. Only activities on the critical path may qualify. Extensions do not apply if accounted for in original contract time. Extensions cover additional rainy/unworkable days beyond predetermined levels, major calamities, non-delivery of materials or permits, and other meritorious causes approved by authorized engineers and procuring entities.

instruction: What is the role of accredited testing laboratories in government infrastructure projects?
output: The BRS of DPWH, DOST, or DTI accredits testing laboratories based on industry guidelines. Only test results from these accredited laboratories are accepted by government infrastructure project owners to ensure material quality.

instruction: What is the scope and process of contractor performance evaluation in government infrastructure projects?
output: All Procuring Entities must evaluate contractors using NEDA-approved Constructors Performance Evaluation System (CPES) Guidelines during construction and upon completion, including all government projects regardless of amount or funding. Procuring Entities must budget for CPES implementation. For projects lacking specific CPES guidelines, constituent agencies may adopt their own with NEDA-INFRACOM approval.

instruction: What mechanisms and responsibilities exist for CPES implementation?
output: Procuring Entities establish CPES Implementing Units responsible for implementing CPES guidelines, accrediting and managing Constructors Performance Evaluators (CPEs), and evaluating CPEs yearly. CPES results are submitted monthly to CIAP, maintained in databanks, disseminated within agencies and to interested users, and used for contractor pre-qualification, awarding, project monitoring, policy-making, and performance improvement.

instruction: What general contract implementation aspects are included in GPPB manuals for infrastructure procurement?
output: GPPB manuals cover subcontracting, traffic and property interference, site clearance, inspections and testing, daywork, work measurement, and other aspects relevant to contract implementation.

instruction: What are the provisions for advance payment in consulting services procurement under Annex F?
output: Advance payment up to 15% of the contract amount may be allowed to consultants for mobilization costs upon submission of an irrevocable standby letter of credit from an acceptable entity. The payment is repaid from progress payments as agreed during contract negotiations and fully liquidated within the contract duration.

instruction: What is stipulated regarding the cost structure of consulting services contracts?
output: Consulting services contracts are fixed price, and any extension of contract time shall not involve additional cost.

instruction: What other rules and guidelines apply to consulting services contract implementation?
output: Further rules and regulations for consulting services implementation shall be included in GPPB-issued manuals but are not detailed in the excerpt provided.

instruction: What is the policy on the use of alternative methods of procurement according to the 2016 Revised IRR Annex H?
output: All procurement shall generally be through competitive bidding. However, alternative methods may be used in exceptional cases justified under R.A. 9184 and its IRR, with prior approval of the Head of the Procuring Entity (HoPE) upon BAC recommendation. The Procuring Entity must ensure obtaining the most advantageous price to the government.

instruction: What is the scope and applicability of the guidelines for alternative methods of procurement under Annex H?
output: The guidelines apply to national government agencies, branches, constitutional offices, departments, bureaus, offices, state universities and colleges, government-owned and controlled corporations, government financial institutions, and local government units, excluding AFP Corps of Engineers projects and certain alternative procurement types such as limited source bidding, negotiated procurement under defense cooperation, NGO and community participation, and UN agencies procurement.

instruction: What restrictions apply regarding splitting of government contracts in alternative procurement?
output: Splitting contracts into smaller quantities, amounts, phases, or sub-contracts to evade competitive bidding and its requirements is prohibited. For phased infrastructure projects, clear delineation of work that is usable and structurally sound is required, with detailed engineering for each phase as outlined in Annex A.

instruction: What confidentiality rules govern bidding documents under alternative procurement?
output: Bidding documents are strictly confidential until advertised or posted, except to authorized personnel. In procurements affecting national security, disclosure depends on the HoPE's discretion considering sensitivity and confidentiality in relation to the request's purpose.

instruction: What are the requirements for advertisement and posting of procurement opportunities in alternative procurement?
output: Advertisement in newspapers and posting may be dispensed with. However, for shopping of ordinary office supplies (ABC above ₱50,000), two failed biddings, and small value procurement (ABC above ₱50,000), the BAC must post notices on PhilGEPS, Procuring Entity website if available, and a conspicuous place at the Procuring Entity premises for at least three calendar days.

instruction: What mandatory documents must suppliers or consultants submit in alternative procurement?
output: Suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, contractors, and consultants must submit required documents enumerated in Appendix A of the guidelines. For negotiated procurement in emergency cases, expired permits with renewal receipts and unnotarized omnibus sworn statements may be conditionally accepted with post-award compliance.

instruction: What is the role of PhilGEPS registration in alternative methods of procurement?
output: PhilGEPS registration and providing a registration number is mandatory for award eligibility in specified alternative methods, including direct contracting, certain shopping cases, take-over of contracts (new bidders), scientific or specialized work, highly technical consultants, small value procurement, and lease of real property and venue.

instruction: When and how should observers be involved in alternative procurement?
output: Observers must be invited in negotiated procurement following two failed biddings per Section 13 of the IRR. For other alternative methods, observers may be invited at the Procuring Entity's discretion.

instruction: What is the rule on reference to brand names in alternative procurement?
output: Specifications must be based on characteristics, functionality, or performance. Brand name references are only allowed for equipment compatible with existing fleet or to maintain performance and lifespan, applicable also to goods in infrastructure projects and consulting services.

instruction: Who may conduct Shopping and Negotiated Procurement under specific alternative methods by delegation?
output: Through BAC resolution and HoPE approval, these may be delegated to End-user units or appropriate departments. For urgent Shopping and certain Negotiated Procurement, BAC and HoPE may further delegate to specific officials or offices for efficient procurement management, except BAC Chairperson or members or conflicted officials.

instruction: What must the BAC do if insufficient quotations or proposals are received repeatedly in alternative procurement?
output: The BAC must conduct a mandatory review and evaluation of terms, conditions, specifications, and cost estimates. Based on findings, it may revise these and adjust the ABC with required approvals before repeating the procurement process.

instruction: What are the procedures for Notice of Award, contract approval, and Notice to Proceed in alternative procurement?
output: Except for Shopping, Negotiated Procurement (Emergency Cases), Agency-to-Agency, and Small Value Procurement, the BAC recommends award to HoPE who must approve or disapprove within 15 calendar days. Upon approval, the NOA is issued immediately. The supplier must enter contract upon NOA receipt; the contract signed by HoPE or authorized representative after documentary compliance. NTP and approved contract copies must be issued within 3 calendar days after government approval. NOA, contract, and NTP must be posted on PhilGEPS, Procuring Entity websites, and premises within 10 days, except for contracts with ABC ≤ ₱50,000.

instruction: What are the rules regarding bid, performance, and warranty securities in alternative procurement?
output: Bid security may be dispensed with except in Limited Source Bidding. Performance and warranty securities are required as per Sections 39 and 62 of the IRR for methods including Two-Failed Biddings, Emergency Cases (Infrastructure Projects), Take-over of Contracts, Adjacent/Contiguous Infrastructure Projects, and Small Value Procurement (Infrastructure Projects). Warranty securities are not required for Consulting Services.

instruction: What is the effect of blacklisting on suppliers, contractors, or consultants in government procurement?
output: Suspended or blacklisted parties are barred from participating in all government procurement opportunities during the suspension or blacklisting period, regardless of procurement modality, following the Uniform Guidelines for Blacklisting issued by the GPPB.

instruction: What is direct contracting and under what conditions is it allowed according to Annex H?
output: Direct contracting involves procurement without elaborate bidding documents by requesting a price quotation or pro-forma invoice from a single supplier, accepted immediately or after negotiation. It is allowed for proprietary goods obtainable only from one source, critical components necessary for contractor performance guarantees, or exclusive dealership items without suitable substitutes at better terms. Industry surveys justifying direct contracting must precede procurement.

instruction: What is the procedure for direct contracting?
output: The BAC prepares the request for quotation or pro-forma invoice with terms and sends it to the identified supplier. Simplified negotiations ensure supplier capability and advantageous pricing. BAC recommends award to HoPE, who approves and issues the award as per procedural rules.

instruction: What constitutes a repeat order and what are its conditions under the 2016 Revised IRR Annex H?
output: Repeat orders replenish goods from the original competitive bidding award under these conditions: unit prices same or lower than original contract and still advantageous after price verification; no contract or purchase order splitting; orders within six months from original Notice to Proceed with partial accepted deliveries; orders not exceeding 25% of original contract quantity; goods must be quantifiable, divisible, and at least four units per item.

instruction: What is the procedure for repeat orders?
output: The End-User prepares a purchase request with market price studies and justification. The BAC recommends the repeat order award to the HoPE. Award follows Section IV(L) of the guidelines, ensuring compliance with procurement rules.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 1, what do the Guidelines for Design and Build Infrastructure Projects supplement?
output: These guidelines shall govern the procurement and implementation of contracts for design and build infrastructure projects and shall supplement applicable provisions of Republic Act No. 9184 and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations, in particular Section 17.6 and Annex E.

instruction: What is the purpose of the Design and Build Guidelines according to Annex G Section 2?
output: These guidelines are formulated to determine the conditions for the use of the design and build scheme for infrastructure projects and the procedures for the implementation thereof.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 3.1, what is one advantage of the design and build scheme regarding responsibility?
output: Since both design and construction are in the hands of the contractor, there is a single point of responsibility for quality, cost, and schedule adherence, including the risks related to design. This precludes buck-passing and finger-pointing between the designer and the builder.

instruction: What time advantage does the design and build scheme offer according to Annex G Section 3.1(b)?
output: Because design and construction periods can overlap, the total design and construction time, as well as the final project cost, will be significantly reduced.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 3.2(a), what is a disadvantage of the design and build scheme?
output: In utilizing the design and build scheme for a particular project, contractors are given too much discretion in determining the project cost and there is difficulty in predicting its final cost until the actual commencement of construction. However, this can be addressed by prescribing that the bid/contract price should not exceed the ABC and that the contract price is a fixed lump sum amount.

instruction: What is the Approved Budget for the Contract in design and build projects according to Annex G Section 4(a)?
output: The ABC shall be a lump sum amount that shall cover the cost of design and construction works based on the conceptual design and performance specifications and in accordance with applicable provisions of the law or agency guidelines. The ABC shall be calculated based on either the approximate quantities of work of the conceptual design, from standardized designs or from cost records of previous projects of similar kind.

instruction: What are Design and Build Projects according to Annex G Section 4(d)?
output: Design and Build Projects refer to infrastructure projects where the procuring entity awards a single contract for the architectural/engineering design and construction to a single firm, partnership, corporation, joint venture or consortium.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 4(e), what are Performance Specifications and Parameters?
output: The procuring entity shall define the required performance specifications and criteria and its means of measurement based on the operating outputs and in accordance with appropriate design and construction standards, legal and technical obligations and any other relevant government commitments as required by existing laws and regulations. It shall not be drawn up to favor a particular solution, design and construction method.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 5.1(a), when may the Design and Build scheme be applied?
output: The Design and Build scheme shall be applied for flagship, priority and fast track projects that need to be completed on a tight completion schedule, as included in the Medium-Term Public Investment Program (MTPIP) for national projects and in the Regional Development Investment Plan (RDIP) for regional and provincial projects.

instruction: When may design and build be used for infrastructure projects with advanced technology according to Annex G Section 5.1(b)?
output: For infrastructure projects requiring advanced engineering or construction technologies or whose intellectual property rights belong to private companies, the Design and Build scheme shall be applied.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 5.1(d), when may design and build be used for small projects?
output: For small projects where there are previously approved drawings or standardized designs and an innovation in design and construction methods under the design and build scheme will result in lower costs and higher quality projects. Examples of these are school buildings, rural health units, among others.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 5.2, what approval is required for design and build projects?
output: All design and build projects shall be included in the Annual Procurement Plan (APP) of the procuring entity concerned and shall be subject to prior approval by the Head of the Procuring Entity or his/her duly authorized representative.

instruction: What is the Design and Build Committee according to Annex G Section 6?
output: The procuring entity may create a Design and Build Committee (DBC) composed of highly technical personnel experienced in the field of architecture, engineering and construction in the particular type of project to be bid. The DBC shall assist the PMO in the preparation of conceptual design and performance specifications, review of detailed engineering design and supervision of the project, and assist the BAC and TWG in evaluation of technical proposals.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 7, what preliminary studies are required before bidding for design and build contracts?
output: No bidding and award of design and build contracts shall be made unless the required preliminary design and construction studies have been sufficiently carried out and duly approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity. These shall include: Project Description; Conceptual Design; Performance Specifications and Parameters; Preliminary Survey and Mapping; Preliminary Investigations; Utility Locations; Approved Budget for the Contract; Proposed Design and Construction Schedule; Minimum requirements for Construction Safety and Health Program; and Tender/Bidding Documents.

instruction: Who is responsible for right-of-way acquisition in design and build projects according to Annex G Section 7?
output: The acquisition of right-of-way and the conduct of eminent domain proceedings shall still be the responsibility of the procuring entity, which shall include a preliminary budget for this purpose.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 8.1, what is the winning bidder's responsibility after contract award?
output: Upon award of the design and build contract, the winning bidder shall be responsible for the preparation and submission of all necessary detailed engineering investigations, surveys and designs in accordance with the provisions of Annex A of the IRR (with the exception of the Bidding Documents and the ABC).

instruction: According to Annex G Section 8.3, who is ultimately responsible for the detailed engineering design?
output: The design and build contractor shall be solely responsible for the integrity of the detailed engineering design and the performance of the structure irrespective of the approval/confirmation by the procuring entity.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 9.2(ii)(a), what is the experience requirement for design and build contractors?
output: In the technical requirements, the design and build contractor (as solo or in joint venture/consortia) should be able to comply with the experience requirement under the IRR of R.A. 9184, where one of the parties (in a joint venture/consortia) should have at least one similar project, both in design and construction, with at least 50% of the cost of the ABC.

instruction: Can a bidder without design and build experience participate according to Annex G Section 9.2(ii)(b)?
output: Yes, if the bidder has no experience in design and build projects on its own it may enter into subcontracting, partnerships, or joint venture with design or engineering firms for the design portion of the contract.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 9.2(ii)(c), what is the minimum Filipino ownership requirement for design and build joint ventures?
output: Joint ventures/consortia among Filipino contractors and consultants or among Filipino contractors and foreign consultants shall be allowed, provided that Filipino ownership or interest thereof shall be at least seventy five percent (75%). Joint ventures where Filipino ownership is less than 75% may be eligible where structures require techniques not adequately possessed by Filipinos and Filipino ownership is not less than twenty-five percent (25%).

instruction: According to Annex G Section 10.1, what additional documents must be included in the first envelope for design and build projects?
output: The first envelope (Technical Proposal) shall contain all required documents for infrastructure projects under Section 25.2(b) of the IRR and the following additional documents: Preliminary Conceptual Design Plans; Design and construction methods; List of design and construction personnel with complete qualification and experience data; and Value engineering analysis of design and construction method.

instruction: What must the second envelope contain according to Annex G Section 10.2?
output: The second envelope (Financial Proposal) shall contain all required documents for infrastructure projects under Section 25.3 of the IRR and the following additional documents: Lump sum bid prices including detailed engineering cost in the prescribed Bid Form; Detailed estimates including a summary sheet indicating unit prices of construction materials, labor rates and equipment rentals; and Cash flow by the quarter and payments schedule.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 11.1, what is evaluated in the first-step procedure for design and build bids?
output: The first step of evaluation shall involve review of preliminary conceptual designs and track record using non-discretionary 'pass/fail' criteria involving compliance with: adherence of preliminary design plans to required performance specifications; concept of approach and methodology for detailed engineering; and quality of personnel to be assigned to the project.

instruction: When may oral presentations be required according to Annex G Section 11.1(ii)?
output: For complex or unique undertakings, such as those involving highly specialized or advanced engineering technology, eligible bidders may be required, at the option of the agency concerned, to make an oral presentation within fifteen (15) calendar days after the deadline for submission of technical proposals.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 11.2, what happens in the second-step evaluation procedure?
output: Only bids that passed the first step criteria shall be subjected to the second step. The BAC shall open the financial proposal of each 'passed' bidder and evaluate it using non-discretionary criteria including arithmetical corrections. The BAC shall automatically disqualify any total calculated bid price which exceeds the ABC. Total calculated bid prices shall be ranked in ascending order, and the bid with the lowest total calculated bid price shall be identified as the Lowest Calculated Bid (LCB).

instruction: According to Annex G Section 12.1, what happens to the LCB after evaluation?
output: The LCB shall be subject to post-qualification in accordance with Section 34, Rule X of the IRR to determine its responsiveness to the eligibility and bid requirements. If after post-qualification the Lowest Calculated Bid is determined to be post-qualified it shall be considered the Lowest Calculated and Responsive Bid (LCRB) and the contract shall be awarded to the bidder.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 12.2, how long does the Head of the Procuring Entity have to approve or disapprove the BAC's recommendation?
output: The Head of the Procuring Entity shall approve or disapprove the recommendations of the BAC within a period not exceeding fifteen (15) calendar days from the determination and declaration by the BAC of the LCRB.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.1, when can works commence in design and build contracts?
output: No works shall commence unless the contractor has submitted the required documentary requirements and the procuring entity has given written approval. Work execution shall be in accordance with reviewed and approved documents.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.3, when must the contractor submit a detailed program of work?
output: The Contractor shall submit a detailed program of work within fourteen (14) calendar days after the issuance of the Notice to Proceed for approval by the procuring entity.

instruction: What must the detailed program of work include according to Annex G Section 13.3?
output: The detailed program of work shall include: the order in which work will be carried out including timing for each stage; periods for review of outputs and approvals; sequence for inspections and tests; general description of design and construction methods; number and names of personnel for each stage; list of equipment required; and description of quality control system.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.4, who bears the cost of rectifying errors in submitted documents?
output: Any errors, omissions, inconsistencies, inadequacies or failure submitted by the contractor that do not comply with the requirements shall be rectified, resubmitted and reviewed at the contractor's cost. If the Contractor wishes to modify any previously approved design or document, the contractor shall notify the procuring entity and shall shoulder the cost of such changes.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.5(i), who pays for change orders resulting from contractor design errors?
output: Change Orders resulting from design errors, omissions or non-conformance with the performance specifications and parameters and the contract documents by the contractor shall be implemented by the contractor at no additional cost to the procuring entity.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.5(ii), what is the contractor entitled to for changes in procuring entity's specifications?
output: Provided that the contractor suffers delay and/or incurs costs due to changes or errors in the procuring entity's performance specifications and parameters, he shall be entitled to either: an extension of time for such delays under Section 10 of Annex E; or payment for such costs as specified in the contract documents, provided that the cumulative amount of the variation order does not exceed ten percent (10%) of the original contract price.

instruction: Is the contractor entitled to advance payment in design and build projects according to Annex G Section 13.7?
output: Yes, the contractor shall be entitled to advance payment subject to the provisions of Section 4 of Annex E.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.10, what is the minimum Defects Liability Period for design and build projects?
output: All design and build projects shall have a minimum Defects Liability Period of one (1) year after contract completion or as provided for in the contract documents. This is without prejudice to the liabilities imposed upon the engineer/architect who drew up the plans and specification for a building sanctioned under Article 1723 of the New Civil Code of the Philippines.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.11, what is the contractor's liability for structural defects?
output: The contractor shall be held liable for design and structural defects and/or failure of the completed project within the warranty periods specified in Section 62.2.3.2 of the IRR.

instruction: What is a Conceptual Design according to Annex G Section 4(c)?
output: Conceptual Design shall describe the general idea of the procuring entity with regard to the completed facility and shall identify the scope or physical components and structures, specific outputs and requirements of the structures and proposed methods of construction, where necessary.

instruction: What are Preliminary Investigations according to Annex G Section 4(f)?
output: Preliminary Investigations shall include, among others, information on soil, geotechnical, hydrologic, hydraulic, seismic, traffic, and environmental conditions that shall be used to define project design criteria, to set the basis for any changed conditions and establish preliminary project cost estimates.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.2, what is the contractor responsible for regarding project information?
output: The contractor shall be responsible for obtaining all necessary information as to risks, contingencies and other circumstances which may affect the works and shall prepare and submit all necessary documents specified by the procuring entity to meet all regulatory approvals as specified in the contract documents.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.8, who defines the quality control procedures?
output: The procuring entity shall define the quality control procedures for the design and construction in accordance with agency guidelines and shall issue the proper certificates of acceptance for sections of the works or the whole of the works as provided for in the contract documents.

instruction: According to Annex G Section 13.9, what must the contractor provide for specified tests?
output: The contractor shall provide all necessary equipment, personnel, instruments, documents and others to carry out specified tests.

instruction: What authority does the GPPB have regarding these guidelines according to Annex G Section 14?
output: In the implementation of these guidelines, the GPPB may issue additional guidelines or introduce modifications thereto through the amendment of its specific provisions as the need arises, as well as formulate, approve and disseminate standard Bidding Documents, forms and evaluation documents, whenever necessary.

instruction: What are the purposes and key provisions of the Guidelines on Termination of Contracts under Annex I of the 2016 Revised IRR?
output: The guidelines promote fairness in terminating government procurement contracts for goods, infrastructure, and consulting services, prescribing contract conditions and protective measures. Definitions cover coercive, collusive, corrupt, and fraudulent practices. Grounds for termination include default (e.g., failure to deliver or significant negative slippage), convenience, insolvency, unlawful acts, and contractor/consultant-initiated termination. Procedures mandate verification by the Implementing Unit, issuance of a Notice to Terminate with show cause opportunity, decision by the Head of Procuring Entity within 10 calendar days, and possible formation of a Contract Termination Review Committee.

instruction: What are the specific grounds for termination of contracts for goods under the 2016 Revised IRR Annex I?
output: Termination for default may occur if the supplier fails to deliver at least 10% of the goods within the specified period or extension (excluding force majeure), or is unable to deliver at least 10% of goods for 60 calendar days post force majeure, or fails any other contractual obligation.

instruction: Under what circumstances may the procuring entity terminate infrastructure project contracts for default?
output: Termination occurs if the contractor incurs negative slippage of 15% or more during project execution, negative slippage of 10% or more after contract expiry, abandons or refuses to proceed after valid notice, lacks essential equipment on site, fails to execute work per contract, refuses to remove defective materials, or sublets work without approval.

instruction: What are the procedures for termination initiated by contractors or consultants?
output: Contractors may terminate infrastructure contracts if work stops for 60 continuous days due to procuring entity failures like non-provision of supplies or adverse peace and order certified by authorities. Consultants may terminate if the procuring entity materially breaches contract obligations and fails to remedy within 60 days after notice.

instruction: Describe the process for issuing a Notice to Terminate a government procurement contract.
output: Upon Implementing Unit recommendation and verified report, the Head of Procuring Entity issues a written Notice to Terminate stating grounds, extent (full or partial), instructions to show cause within 7 calendar days, and any special instructions. The notice includes the verified report.

instruction: What happens if the supplier/contractor does not respond to the Notice to Terminate?
output: If no verified position paper is submitted within 7 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Terminate, the Head of Procuring Entity shall issue an order terminating the contract.

instruction: Under what condition may the Procuring Entity rescind the Notice of Termination?
output: The Procuring Entity may withdraw the Notice of Termination before receiving the supplier/contractor’s verified position paper if it determines that the work or items subject to termination had been completed or performed before receipt of the notice.

instruction: What are the timelines and authority related to the termination decision?
output: The Head of Procuring Entity must decide on termination within a non-extendible 10 calendar days from receipt of the verified position paper and notify the supplier/contractor in writing. Termination is effective upon receipt of the notice and limited to grounds in the Notice to Terminate.

instruction: What is the role of the Contract Termination Review Committee (CTRC)?
output: The Head of Procuring Entity may create a CTRC to assist in termination functions. The CTRC’s decisions require Head of Procuring Entity’s approval.

instruction: What options does the Procuring Entity have after contract termination for convenience in contracts for goods?
output: Goods completed or ready within 30 calendar days after termination notice shall be accepted at contract terms. For undelivered goods, the Procuring Entity may accept partially delivered work and pay agreed amounts, or cancel and compensate for costs like raw materials purchased if proven by the supplier under oath.

instruction: What notice requirements exist for contractor- or consultant-initiated termination?
output: Contractors/consultants must serve written notice to the Procuring Entity at least 30 calendar days before intended termination. Contract termination is effective if the contractor/consultant does not resume work within 30 days after notice receipt.

instruction: What guidelines govern infrastructure projects undertaken 'by administration' as per Appendix 1?
output: Infrastructure projects 'by administration' are implemented under agency supervision via own personnel, applicable to NGAs, GOCCs, GFIs, SUCs, and LGUs, excluding AFP Corps of Engineers governed by separate guidelines.

instruction: What conditions must implementing agencies meet to undertake infrastructure projects by administration?
output: They must have completed or supervised similar projects at least 50% the cost of the current project and own or have access to necessary tools and equipment. For LGUs with national funding, DPWH validates these capabilities.

instruction: What labor contracting systems are permitted under infrastructure projects by administration?
output: In-house labor via plantilla positions, job-order contracts governed by COA or CSC rules, and the pakyaw contracting system involving community labor groups may be used.

instruction: Describe the pakyaw contracting system for infrastructure projects by administration.
output: Pakyaw labor is recruited locally according to skill level, with barangay leaders involved in group formation. Groups compete by offering lowest rates per output for lump sum work. Groups have elected leaders signing contracts, may not include licensed contractors or labor supplied by labor-only contractors, and contracts per group must not exceed ₱500,000.

instruction: Describe the electronic bid submission and modification process.
output: On-line Bidders submit bids via their Online Nominee before the deadline, with electronic bid submission time recorded by PhilGEPS server as official time. Bids may be modified electronically before closing. Withdrawal is allowed before bid submission deadline. After closing, PhilGEPS bars further submissions.

instruction: What are the bid security submission requirements under electronic bidding?
output: On-line bidders may submit cash bid security electronically. For other forms, a scanned copy must accompany the bid electronically, but the original must be submitted to the BAC by the close of business on bid submission day or the bid is non-compliant. Original bid securities sent by registered mail or courier are accepted on the receipt date by the BAC, subject to post-qualification verification.

instruction: What are the rules for bid opening in electronic bidding?
output: Manually filed bids are recorded and input in PhilGEPS with submission details before opening. BAC opens bids immediately post deadline. Bid openers and BAC members login securely to PhilGEPS; decryption requires quorum. Manual envelope bids are publicly opened for eligibility evaluation using pass/fail criteria. After manual opening and encoding, electronic bids are decrypted and similarly examined. Second envelopes (financials) of passed bidders are opened the same day. Non-compliant or over-ABC bids are failed. PhilGEPS notifies failed bidders.

instruction: Explain how bid evaluation and ranking are conducted using PhilGEPS for goods and infrastructure projects.
output: The BAC evaluates all bids using non-discretionary criteria, checking completeness and correcting arithmetic errors. Bids must include all applicable taxes. Discrepancies between prices and quantities are resolved in favor of detailed bid documents. Bids exceeding ABC are disqualified. After evaluation, bids are ranked ascendingly by total calculated price to identify the Lowest Calculated Bid (LCB). The BAC signs and uploads an Abstract of Bids. The Abstract is manually approved by the BAC and posted on PhilGEPS, notifying all bidders electronically.

instruction: What procedures does PhilGEPS follow for post-qualification following bid evaluation?
output: The bidder with LCB or Highest Rated Bid (HRB) is notified by email to submit post-qualification documents within three calendar days. The BAC evaluates and, if the bidder passes, declares it Lowest Calculated Responsive Bid (LCRB) or Highest Rated Responsive Bid (HRRB) and recommends award to HoPE. If the bidder fails, the BAC notifies and conducts post-qualification for next ranked bidder until one passes or bidding fails. The process is completed within seven days, extendable up to thirty days by HoPE. Results are recorded in PhilGEPS and all bidders notified electronically.

instruction: Summarize the contract award process in electronic bidding as per the 2016 Revised IRR Annex 3.
output: After post-qualification, the BAC recommends award to the HoPE with supporting documents including resolution, Abstract of Bids, program of work, approvals, and other legal documents. The HoPE has 15 calendar days to approve or deny the recommendation, providing written grounds if denied. Upon approval, the Notice of Award (NOA) is created and issued via PhilGEPS if no protests are pending. The NOA issuance triggers automatic notification to all bidders. Contract award requires submission of valid JVAs (if applicable), performance security, contract signing, and higher authority approval, concluding within the bid validity period. The NOA is posted on PhilGEPS within 3 days.

instruction: What is the Government of the Philippines-Official Merchants Registry (GoP-OMR) and its purpose according to the Revised IRR of RA 9184?
output: The GoP-OMR is a centralized electronic database of manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, contractors, and consultants maintained by PhilGEPS, designed to serve as the official registry for government electronic procurement to promote transparency and efficiency.

instruction: Does registration in the GoP-OMR automatically confer eligibility to participate in public bidding?
output: No, registration and membership in the GoP-OMR do not automatically confer eligibility to participate in public bidding; eligibility is determined solely by the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC).

instruction: What are the requirements for a merchant’s registration in the GoP-OMR?
output: Requirements include a duly accomplished PhilGEPS Registration Form, a bank account number, a secure email address, a digital certificate (when available), eligibility requirements per R.A. 9184 and its Revised IRR, and a certification verifying authenticity and completeness of submitted documents.

instruction: What is the validity period of the Certificate of Registration and Membership in the GoP-OMR, and what happens if updates are not made?
output: The Certificate is valid for one year from issuance and may be renewed or updated; failure to update records causes automatic suspension of the certificate's validity until compliance.

instruction: How does the PhilGEPS office handle applications for registration in the GoP-OMR?
output: PhilGEPS receives and processes all applications, and has the exclusive authority to approve or disapprove registrations based on compliance with the guidelines and existing laws.

instruction: What happens if a merchant is blacklisted by a procuring entity or foreign entities recognized by the Government Procurement Policy Board?
output: The PhilGEPS office shall deny or exclude the merchant from the GoP-OMR by canceling their account, upon receipt of a blacklisting order from the procuring entity or recognition of foreign blacklisting.

instruction: What are the general guidelines for using existing merchant registries when integrating with the GoP-OMR?
output: All existing electronic merchant registries used by procuring entities shall be integrated into the GoP-OMR; if incompatible, the prior registry shall be discontinued in favor of GoP-OMR. Manual registries may be retained temporarily but should shift to GoP-OMR when transitioning to electronic registries.

instruction: What funding sources are authorized for payment of honoraria to government personnel involved in procurement under Budget Circular No. 2004-5A?
output: Authorized sources include proceeds from sale of bid documents, fees from contractor/supplier registry, fees for copies of BAC documents, protest fees, liquidated damages, and proceeds from bid or performance security forfeiture.

instruction: Under Budget Circular No. 2004-5A, when are government personnel entitled to honoraria for procurement activities?
output: Honoraria are payable only for successfully completed procurement projects involving competitive bidding, specifically upon contract award to the winning bidder.

instruction: What are the maximum honoraria rates for personnel involved in procurement, and which personnel are excluded from honoraria?
output: Maximum rates per completed project are ₱3,000 for BAC Chair, ₱2,500 for BAC Members, and ₱2,000 for TWG Chair and Members. Personnel whose positions are in the Procurement Unit, and Department Undersecretaries or Assistant Secretaries serving in BAC, are excluded from honoraria.

instruction: What guidelines govern the sale of bidding documents as per Section 17.4 of the IRR of RA 9184?
output: Bidding documents shall be sold at standard fixed rates corresponding to the Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC), and the price must be included in the Invitation to Bid to inform prospective bidders.

instruction: What are the maximum costs of bidding documents based on the Approved Budget for the Contract?
output: The maximum bidding document fees are ₱500 for contracts up to ₱500,000; ₱1,000 for ₱500,001 to ₱1 million; ₱5,000 for ₱1 million to ₱5 million; ₱10,000 for ₱5 million to ₱10 million; ₱25,000 for ₱10 million to ₱50 million; ₱50,000 for ₱50 million to ₱500 million; and ₱75,000 for contracts above ₱500 million.

instruction: What happens to the proceeds from the sale of bidding documents?
output: Proceeds are used for payment of honoraria as provided in Budget Circular No. 2004-5A or to augment funds for legal assistance and indemnification of BAC members and support staff.

instruction: What is the general policy regarding the eligibility of foreign suppliers, contractors, and consultants in Philippine government procurement?
output: The general policy, as provided by Republic Act No. 9184 and Republic Act No. 5183, is to prefer Filipino nationals for government procurement contracts, but qualified foreign nationals may participate if domestic preference, Most-Favored Nation status, and non-discrimination provisions under relevant laws and treaties are followed.

instruction: Under what circumstances may foreign suppliers participate in procurement of goods according to the Appendix 9 Guidelines and the Revised IRR of R.A. 9184?
output: Foreign suppliers may participate when goods are not available from local suppliers, to prevent anti-competitive situations, when reciprocity rights allow, or when covered by treaty or international agreement.

instruction: What is required for a procuring entity to invite foreign suppliers when goods are not available locally?
output: The head of the procuring entity must certify, after diligent market research, that no local supplier can provide the required goods and may also need certifications from appropriate government regulatory bodies depending on the goods.

instruction: How may foreign contractors be eligible for infrastructure projects under the Revised IRR of RA 9184?
output: Foreign contractors can join if allowed under a treaty or international/executive agreement or by forming a joint venture with local contractors with foreign ownership not exceeding 25%, and in cases requiring specialized techniques not available locally.

instruction: What is the reciprocity rule in government procurement of goods?
output: Foreign suppliers from countries granting Filipino nationals reciprocal rights to participate in public procurement may also participate in Philippine government procurement, provided they submit certification from their government and it is validated during post-qualification.

instruction: What is a Bid Securing Declaration under RA 9184?
output: A Bid Securing Declaration is an undertaking by a bidder to pay a fine and accept disqualification or suspension if procurement rules are violated, serving as an alternative to bid security forms specified in Section 27.2 of the IRR.

instruction: For how long is a Bid Securing Declaration valid and when does it expire?
output: It is valid for a period indicated in the bidding documents not exceeding 120 calendar days from bid opening and automatically expires upon bidding period expiration, disqualification of all bidders, or contract award and furnishing of performance security by the winning bidder.

instruction: What penalties apply to bidders violating a Bid Securing Declaration?
output: Violators face a two-year disqualification from government procurement and a fine calculated based on a fixed percentage or the difference between their bid and the ABC or next lowest bid, depending on the scenario.

instruction: What is Limited Source Bidding and when may it be used under RA 9184 and its IRR?
output: Limited Source Bidding is an alternative procurement method used only in highly exceptional and justifiable cases, such as procurement of highly specialized goods or consulting services where only a few qualified suppliers or consultants are known, or for major plant components to maintain uniform quality.

instruction: What is the procedure for pre-selection of suppliers or consultants in Limited Source Bidding according to GPPB Resolution 05-2011?
output: The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) prepares a pre-selected list of suppliers or consultants from a government-maintained list or, if unavailable, requests such a list from a relevant authority or self-generates one if the procuring entity has expertise, evaluating entities based on capability, personnel, equipment, and financial position, subject to Head of Procuring Entity (HOPE) approval and submission to the GPPB.

instruction: What must the pre-selected list include and who approves it?
output: The pre-selected list must include the technical specifications or terms of reference and the evaluation criteria used, and must be approved by the Head of the Procuring Entity (HOPE).

instruction: What happens after the HOPE approves the pre-selected list in Limited Source Bidding?
output: The HOPE transmits the pre-selected list with justifications and certifications to the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB), which posts the list on its or PhilGEPS website for transparency.

instruction: What should the procuring entity do if no relevant government authority exists for the pre-selection list?
output: The procuring entity may prepare a self-generated list if it can establish expertise on the procurement subject; otherwise, it must resort to open competitive bidding.

instruction: How long must the procurement opportunity for Limited Source Bidding be posted?
output: Procurement opportunities must be posted conspicuously and on PhilGEPS for seven (7) calendar days after GPPB-TSO acknowledgment of the pre-selected list.

instruction: Are the rules of competitive bidding applicable to Limited Source Bidding?
output: Yes, except for posting requirements specific to Limited Source Bidding, the procurement must follow the rules prescribed in RA 9184 and its IRR applicable to competitive bidding.

instruction: When do the guidelines amending the pre-selection procedure for Limited Source Bidding take effect?
output: These guidelines take effect fifteen (15) days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general nationwide circulation, and upon filing three (3) certified copies with the University of the Philippines Law Center.

instruction: What is the scope and application of the Revised Guidelines for Contract Price Escalation under RA 9184?
output: These Guidelines govern requests for price escalation during implementation of goods and infrastructure contracts under extraordinary circumstances pursuant to Section 61 of RA 9184 and its IRR, applying to all government branches, agencies, GOCCs, GFIs, SUCs, and LGUs. Price escalation for consulting services is not allowed.

instruction: How do the Guidelines define 'Price Escalation' and 'Extraordinary Circumstances'?
output: Price Escalation is an increase in contract price during implementation due to 'extraordinary circumstances' as determined by NEDA and approved by GPPB. Extraordinary Circumstances are events during contract implementation causing price escalation as defined by the Civil Code, such as fortuitous events or extraordinary inflation/deflation.

instruction: What are examples of ordinary and extraordinary fortuitous events under the Guidelines?
output: Ordinary fortuitous events include typhoons, thunderstorms, flooding of low areas, and vehicular accidents, while extraordinary fortuitous events include fire, war, pestilence, unusual floods, locusts, and earthquakes.

instruction: What are the two stages in the review process for a request for price escalation?
output: First, a legal parameter review verifies the existence of extraordinary circumstances according to specified Civil Code articles. Second, a technical parameter review assesses if price changes meet statistical thresholds (two standard deviations or at least 10% increase) using appropriate price indices over a 30-month historical period.

instruction: What technical price indices are used for evaluating price escalation requests?
output: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is used first, followed by Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) based on availability, measured against historical 30-month data published by the National Statistics Office or relevant foreign entities.

instruction: What formula is used to compute price escalation for infrastructure projects?
output: Escalation is computed using the fluctuation factor K = a + b (Xi/Xo) + c (Yi/Yo) + ... + n (Ni/No), where a is a fixed 0.15 coefficient for contractor's profit, b, c, etc., are proportional values of pay items totaling 0.85, and X, Y, Z are the current and baseline price indices of labor, materials, and other components.

instruction: When can requests for price escalation be made and for which costs?
output: Requests can be made only for costs already incurred supported by official documents, not for prospective application, and must be spaced at least six months apart from contract effectivity or previous requests, except at contract completion.

instruction: Who must endorse and approve a request for price escalation?
output: The Head of the Procuring Entity must endorse the request with supporting documents to NEDA, who reviews and recommends action to the GPPB, which has final approval authority.

instruction: What happens after contract completion regarding price escalation?
output: The procuring entity calculates any price escalation due considering downward price movements and deducts any overpayment from retention money or warranty security before their expiration.

instruction: Can contract price escalation be paid without GPPB approval?
output: No, payment of contract price escalation must be approved by the GPPB; approval does not validate any irregularity in the procurement process.

instruction: What conditions affect price escalation payments if the project is behind schedule or has advance payments?
output: Escalation on unaccomplished work is based on the price index at the planned completion period and is paid only upon completion and approval. No escalation is granted for work or materials covered by advance payments.

instruction: What is the effectivity date of these Revised Guidelines for Contract Price Escalation?
output: The Guidelines take effect immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general nationwide circulation and filing of three certified copies with the University of the Philippines Law Center.

instruction: What is the policy on foreign-denominated bids, contract prices, and payments using Letters of Credit under RA 9184?
output: All bid prices shall be considered fixed and contracts generally denominated and paid in Philippine currency except when otherwise agreed by the procuring entity. Foreign-denominated contracts and payments through Letters of Credit (LCs) are subject to conditions and procedures to address currency fluctuations and related expenses.

instruction: How should provisional sums for currency fluctuation be prepared in bidding documents?
output: Procuring entities must include a provisional sum, not exceeding 10% of the Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC), in the bidding documents and Annual Procurement Plan to cover possible increases in expenditure due to peso appreciation/depreciation and LC expenses; unused sums revert as savings.

instruction: What rules apply for bid submission and evaluation involving foreign currency?
output: Bids may be wholly local currency, wholly foreign currency, or a combination, with the foreign component limited to imported goods supported by import documents. Foreign currency bids are converted to Philippine pesos at the exchange rate prevailing on bid opening for evaluation.

instruction: How are contract prices determined and paid when involving foreign currency?
output: Contracts are generally in Philippine pesos, except when approved otherwise. For competitive bidding, foreign bids are converted at bid opening exchange rates; alternative procurement converts at contract signing rates; repeat orders must have prices equal or lower than the original.

instruction: What provisions govern payments using Letters of Credit (LCs) in foreign contracts?
output: For foreign-funded projects with foreign suppliers, LCs may be opened from government banks; payment is made after delivery and acceptance. Expenses and currency fluctuation risks related to LCs are covered by the provisional sum.

instruction: What expenses related to Letters of Credit are borne by suppliers?
output: All charges for opening LCs and incidental expenses, such as bank commissions, documentary taxes, and cables, are charged to the supplier and must be stated in bidding documents.

instruction: When did the guidelines on procurements involving foreign-denominated bids and Letters of Credit take effect?
output: These guidelines took effect fifteen days after publication in the Official Gazette or a nationwide newspaper and upon filing three certified copies with the University of the Philippines Law Center.

instruction: What is the procedure for blacklisting a contractor during the procurement stage according to the Uniform Guidelines for Blacklisting under RA No. 9184?
output: Any bidder, prospective bidder, or authorized observer may file a written complaint with the BAC to initiate blacklisting. The BAC verifies grounds and notifies the contractor, who may request a hearing and submit a written answer within five days. If found at fault, the BAC recommends suspension and forfeiture of bid security to the Head of the Procuring Entity, who decides within fifteen days. The contractor may file a motion for reconsideration or appeal, and the blacklisting becomes final upon resolution of these with a Blacklisting Order issued thereafter.

instruction: What are the grounds for blacklisting a contractor during the contract implementation stage under RA No. 9184?
output: Blacklisting may be imposed for failure to mobilize work, unsatisfactory compliance with contractual obligations, unauthorized subcontracting, poor performance or quality of deliverables, deliberate abandonment of contract, or unlawful acts related to contract acquisition and implementation. The Head of Procuring Entity issues a Blacklisting Order within seven days of contract termination or verified report, also forfeiting performance security.

instruction: What is the effectivity and duration of the blacklisting penalty under RA No. 9184?
output: The blacklisting penalty lasts one or two years as specified in the Blacklisting Order, starting from its issuance date. Blacklisted persons or entities may not participate in bidding during this suspension period. Multiple offenses result in a two-year blacklisting, which subsumes any previous penalty.

instruction: How is the delisting procedure for blacklisted entities handled according to the Uniform Guidelines for Blacklisting?
output: Blacklisted persons or entities are automatically delisted after the suspension period elapses. Procuring Entities must post Blacklisting Orders on the Online Blacklisting Portal within three calendar days of effectivity, and only the lapse of the penalty period or lawful judicial/quasi-judicial order can remove or lift blacklisting status.

instruction: What information must be included in a Blacklisting Order as per RA No. 9184 guidelines?
output: Blacklisting Orders must include the department/office order or board resolution number, registered business name, address, PhilGEPS registration number, license number if applicable, authorized managing officer, project/contract details, grounds/offenses committed, sanctions imposed with duration, and date of issuance.

instruction: What is the purpose of the Revised Guidelines on Recognition of Umbrella Organization of Consultants (UOC) under RA 9184?
output: The Guidelines set forth the criteria and procedure for recognizing UOCs representing major consulting industry sectors, and outline their duties and responsibilities in fostering industry development and government collaboration.

instruction: What criteria must a UOC meet to be recognized by the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB)?
output: A UOC must cover a wide range of professions in a major sector, accredit its members based on technical and financial qualifications, maintain updated member lists, self-police members, conduct capacity development programs, fight corruption, and assist the Philippine consulting industry in becoming internationally competitive.

instruction: What are the primary duties and responsibilities of a recognized UOC?
output: Key duties include accrediting member consultants, maintaining and certifying updated member lists, implementing continuing capacity programs, regulating members including grievance mechanisms, submitting monthly updates to GPPB, providing technical assistance to GPPB, assigning observers to procurement activities, and supervising member compliance with obligations.

instruction: What documents must an umbrella organization submit for evaluation when applying for UOC recognition?
output: Documents include SEC registration or equivalent, Articles of Incorporation and By-laws, organizational profile and objectives, member lists with contact and professional details, accreditation guidelines, composition of accreditation board, capacity building programs, regulation/policing guidelines including sanctions and dispute resolution mechanisms, and liaison officer details.

instruction: What is the validity period of UOC recognition and how is it reviewed?
output: Recognition is valid for two years, subject to annual performance review and possible random inspections by the GPPB. No challenges to recognition are entertained during this period unless due process leads to suspension or revocation.

instruction: Describe the process for application and publication for a UOC seeking recognition.
output: Applicant UOCs must submit a completed application form with required documents to GPPB-TSO, publish the application in a nationwide newspaper and post it on PhilGEPS for 15 calendar days. Questions or oppositions may be filed within this period, after which GPPB evaluates and either grants recognition or requires revision and additional submissions.

instruction: What are some of the major sectors of the Philippine consulting industry covered by the UOC recognition guidelines?
output: Major sectors include Agriculture, Disaster, Education, Energy, Environment, Finance, Health and Social Welfare, ICT, Infrastructure, Labor and Employment, Law, Management, Sociology, and Other Sectors such as Civil aviation, Military, Tourism, and Transport.

instruction: What are 'Accountable Forms' and which government entities are authorized to print Sensitive High Quality/Volume printing requirements?
output: 'Accountable Forms' are individually identified and secured forms. Recognized Government Printers authorized for printing sensitive high quality/volume requirements include Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, National Printing Office, and APO Production Unit, Inc.

instruction: What steps must procuring entities follow for the procurement of printing services for Accountable Forms?
output: Entities must determine printing needs, prepare technical specifications including security features and timelines, conduct market analysis for ABC, seek PCOO assistance if no RGP can undertake the printing, send RFQs to RGPs, evaluate offers, and engage RGPs via agency-to-agency agreement. Private printers may only be engaged if no RGP is available under specific conditions.

instruction: What restrictions apply to Recognized Government Printers (RGPs) engaged for printing services?
output: RGPs must directly undertake printing services contracted and are prohibited from subcontracting or assigning private printers to perform the work.

instruction: What are the applicable methods for procuring water and electricity services under RA 9184?
output: Procurement of water and electricity services shall be done through direct contracting under Section 50 (c) of the IRR of RA 9184 due to the exclusive franchise granted to service providers, with exceptions for purchases like bottled water and procurement by government as concessionaire.

instruction: What are the procurement guidelines for existing telecommunication lines used by government agencies?
output: Existing contracts with telecommunication providers shall be respected. An annual assessment comparing cost and services must be conducted. If the assessment favors the existing provider, services may be renewed; otherwise, bidding is required. Additional lines may be procured via repeat order even beyond the six-month limit under Section 51 of the IRR.

instruction: How should new telecommunication service contracts be procured if no existing provider is satisfactory or available?
output: If multiple providers operate locally, procurement shall be by competitive public bidding or applicable alternative methods. If only one provider operates, direct contracting is allowed.

instruction: What procurement procedures apply to internet service providers (ISPs) for government agencies?
output: Existing ISP contracts shall be respected. Annual quality and cost-benefit assessment is required. If favored, services may be renewed; if not, bidding is required. New ISP contracts follow the same rules as telecommunications: competitive bidding if multiple providers exist, direct contracting if only one.

instruction: What reportorial requirements apply to procurement of utilities such as water, electricity, telecommunications, and internet services?
output: Procurement of these services must be stated in the procuring entity’s Annual Procurement Plan, including estimated budget and chosen procurement method.
